Split the review loop into responsibility modules with zero behaviour change

trouble run r20260923-163956 · git range 00ba02af..85b4f838

`orchestrator/execution/review.py` (1,993 lines, 97 KB) is one class, `_GroupExecution`, that owns every responsibility a group's execution has: generation lifecycle, the coder↔reviewer round, session records and usage, the merge ladder, escalation and rewrite, surprises and prompt notes. The Unit Recipes brainstorm (R9 `shared-plumbing`) needs those responsibilities as separately importable pieces so a second executor can compose the ones it needs without inheriting the coder loop. This plan does exactly the split and nothing else: **six modules, one composition root, every method body moved byte-for-byte, and the observable behaviour of a run identical.** It is the "measurable beginning" the brainstorm names — the measure is the existing suite (1,935 tests on this branch, 104 s) passing with no test *body* changed, plus a layout test and a live-tier pass proving the new modules are real homes and the heartbeat still beats. Not in scope: `orchestrator/cli.py` (3,258 lines) and `sessions.py` are left alone; no recipe, registry or dispatcher; no rename of `review.py` (that is Plan B's decision, when it becomes the `code` recipe's executor).

Summary

Split the review loop into responsibility modules with zero behaviour change — r20260923-163956

TL;DR

  • All 7 groups completed: review.py went from one 1,993-line class to a 226-line composition root over six mixin modules plus a host Protocol, with every existing test body unchanged (g5-2)

Problems found

Three defects surfaced, none in the code this plan moved.

  • over_merge_ceiling, added to merge_small_groups in 6e68605, was never added to the trace's MergeReason literal; any grouping hitting the merge headroom band crashed in TraceRecorder with a pydantic ValidationError (orchestrator/grouping/trace.py) test_cli_price groups a real plan against live file bytes, so g3's size changes pushed one merge into the band.

  • The report shows g7 as changes_required and u7 as not landed; that verdict is a stale verdict-g1-r1.json from the pre-restart session, which the resumed session's same-id report did not replace — g7 merged (g7)
  • Two live tests already failed on the launch branch: a user-level PreToolUse hook runs uv run inside Landlock and hits EACCES on ~/.cache/uv, masking the kernel denial; and Bash(*python *) now matches under Claude Code 2.1.280 (g7-6)

base-context.md (683 lines)

Base context

Worker ground rules

These rules apply to every coder and reviewer session forked from this base context, for the spec you will be given below and the plan document that follows it.

For coders

  • Work only inside your worktree (your current working directory); never touch paths outside it.
  • Your worktree owns its own environment: dependency changes require uv sync run inside the worktree, and any verification item that imports a new dependency must pass there, in that worktree — never against the parent checkout's environment. Always sync with the project's extras (uv sync --all-extras, or whatever the project's own instructions name): a plain uv sync strips the extras, the optional dependencies disappear from the venv, and tests that import them skip at module level — a green run that verified nothing.
  • Verification outputs, logs, and temporary scripts go in .coder-scratch/ at the root of your worktree — it is git-ignored for you and archived with the group's artifacts. Anything else left untracked in the worktree fails the merge gate: commit it, move it into .coder-scratch/, or delete it before you report.
  • Run long or real verification (a full suite, a pipeline over real data, a render) in the foreground and wait for it. A background task is killed when your session ends its turn, so a verification you backgrounded never finishes and its pass is a guess.
  • Data and large binaries never go through git. Directories that appear in your worktree as symlinks (the run's shared data directories) are shared live with every other group and the integration tree: put downloads, models, corpora and generated media there and read inputs from there. Do not commit any file above ~50 MB; the orchestrator relocates such files out of git for you, but a symlink where you expected a file means exactly that happened.
  • Implement the spec you are given fully — code and tests — following the conventions established above.
  • Commit early and often: after each self-contained step that leaves the worktree in a consistent state (a finished file, a passing unit of work), make a git commit with a clear conventional message. Do not accumulate large uncommitted work — if your session is interrupted, only committed work survives; anything uncommitted is lost when the group restarts. The commit subject must start with the first character of the type, not whitespace — if you're using a heredoc to pass the message, check the exact bytes, since a leading newline or space before the subject line is a common heredoc mistake.
  • If a command is denied for permissions, retry the identical command up to three times total, then stop and report status permission_denied with the denied command verbatim in denied_command. Re-sending the identical command is not a workaround; alternate quoting, alternate spellings, shelling through another interpreter, and subprocess.run substitution for the same command are all banned — they route around the sandbox instead of reporting the block.
  • Verify your work against the verification items you will be given before reporting — for real. A verification item is pass only if you ran it in this worktree against the actual dependency, data, or service it names: a mock, a stub backend, a lazily-imported library that was never installed, or "the unit tests I wrote pass" does not make an item about that library pass. If you could not run an item for real, report it skipped with the reason in its notes — a skipped is honest and recoverable; a false pass is the single worst report you can make, because nothing downstream will ever look again.
  • Your environment is part of your work. If uv sync (with the project's extras) fails, or a dependency the spec relies on cannot be installed or imported in this worktree, first try to fix it (pin, alternative build, version constraint) and commit that fix. If you cannot make the real dependency work, do not design around it and report completed: report status blocked with the exact error in summary. The orchestrator resolves a blocked report (spec rewrite, or a human when one is configured); a silent completed on a fake environment resolves nothing.

For reviewers

  • Compute the diff yourself from git rather than trusting the coder's report: verify claims against the actual code and run the tests the spec calls for.
  • Check the environment before you check the code: confirm uv sync with the project's extras succeeds in this worktree and that every dependency the spec names actually imports here. Then check that at least one verification item exercised the real dependency, data, or service — not a mock or a stub. A report whose every pass rests on mocks of the thing under test is changes_required ("exercise the real X in item N"); a dependency that cannot be made to work at all in this environment is too_hard, stated plainly, never approved.
  • If you need scratch space, use only the directory the round names for it, and do not leave scratch files anywhere else in the worktree — the merge gate requires a clean tree.

Report block rules (both roles)

Every final message ends with EXACTLY ONE <run-report> block, whose body is valid JSON with no trailing commas and no comments, and nothing after the closing tag.

  • A coder's status attribute is one of completed | blocked | failed | needs_input | permission_denied and must match the JSON body's "status" field.
    • Use needs_input only when a decision only a human can make blocks you (an ambiguous requirement, a product trade-off, missing access). Put the single specific question in a top-level "question" field; the run pauses and resumes you with the operator's answer. Do not use it for anything you can resolve yourself.
    • Use permission_denied only after retrying the identical denied command up to three times total. Put the exact command in a top-level "denied_command" field, verbatim, with no paraphrasing or quoting changes. Do not use it for a blocked report — that status is unrelated to permission denials.
    • With permission_denied, also set two top-level fields that say how it was denied, because three unrelated causes look identical from where you stand and each needs a different fix from the operator:
      • "denial_error": the error text you actually saw, verbatim — do not summarize or rephrase it. If nothing came back at all, write exactly no error text was returned; a stated absence is usable, a blank field is not.
      • "denial_source": "tool_refused" if the tool call was refused and the command never ran, or "command_error" if the command ran and failed. You know which one happened and the orchestrator cannot work it out afterwards, so this is the single most useful thing you can report here.
    • Every verification item you were given must appear in "verification_results" with status pass | fail | skipped.
  • A reviewer's status attribute is one of approved | changes_required | too_hard | structural and must match the JSON body's "status" field.
    • approved: the work satisfies the spec and its verification items.
    • changes_required: fixable within this group — list concrete, actionable items in "required_changes".
    • too_hard: the spec cannot be satisfied by iterating here; escalate for a spec rewrite.
    • structural: the group boundaries themselves are wrong (work belongs to or conflicts with another group).
  • Either role may record a surprise: a finding that likely invalidates another group's assignment — an interface mismatch, a missing dependency, work that belongs elsewhere. Record it instead of fixing it yourself: {"kind": "interface_mismatch" | "missing_dependency" | "merge_conflict" | "other", "description": "...", "affected_groups": ["g2"]}

Repo conventions (CLAUDE.md)

smart-mcps

A Claude Code plugin that installs skills and session hooks for codegraph, NotebookLM, and Perplexity.

Plugin structure

This is a Claude Code plugin repository. Hooks and skills are distributed to plugin consumers via auto-discovered files:

Path Purpose
hooks/hooks.json Plugin-level hook registrations (uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT})
hooks/scripts/ Hook implementation scripts (.py and .sh)
skills/ Skill definitions
agents/ Subagent definitions (auto-discovered; .claude/agents symlinks here for local dev)
codegraph_mcp/ FastMCP proxy exposing 6 trimmed codegraph tools (smart-mcps-codegraph)
.mcp.json MCP server registration — serves plugin consumers and local dev (see below)
.claude-plugin/plugin.json Plugin identity (name, version)
.claude/settings.json Project-level hooks for local development (uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)

Adding hooks — always register in both places

Every hook script must be wired up in two files:

  1. hooks/hooks.json — so plugin consumers receive it. Uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.
  2. .claude/settings.json — so it runs locally during development. Uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

Matchers are case-sensitive and PascalCase in both files (e.g. "Edit|Write|MultiEdit", "Bash") — a lowercase matcher silently matches nothing. This applies to every event, including SessionStart (codegraph reindex, formatter bootstrap), not just PostToolUse.

Registering in only one place means either plugin consumers or local dev is broken. Always do both.

MCP servers — one file, not two

The dual-registration rule above does not apply to MCP servers: .claude/settings.json has no mcpServers key (it only approves servers via enabledMcpjsonServers). A single .mcp.json at the repo root covers both audiences, because Claude Code reads it twice:

  • Plugin consumers — auto-discovered as the plugin's ./.mcp.json; tools resolve as mcp__plugin_smart-mcps_codegraph__<tool>.
  • Local dev — read as the project-scoped .mcp.json; tools resolve as mcp__codegraph__<tool>.

Hence "--project", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}". ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is set only for consumers; locally it falls back to . (the server's cwd is the project root). Two constraints worth knowing before editing that line:

  • ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is not available in .mcp.json — only in hooks. Using it yields a "Missing environment variables" warning.
  • Defaults don't nest. ${VAR:-default} works, but ${A:-${B}} does not expand B — it silently passes a literal, which uv may accept when the console script is already on PATH, hiding the bug locally while breaking for consumers.

Never keep working notes in the /tmp scratchpad

The session scratchpad under /tmp is wiped when the Claude Code process restarts — not just at the end of a session. Anything written there is gone without warning.

This has already cost real work: on 2026-07-29 a restart destroyed the accumulated findings and deferred-fix list for two sessions of orchestrator debugging, plus a patch backup of a group's stranded work.

Use /tmp only for genuinely throwaway intermediates. Anything another session would want — findings, deferred-fix lists, handoff notes, backups of uncommitted work — goes somewhere durable:

what where
Run findings, deferred fixes, backups .orchestrator/ — gitignored, survives restarts, never collides with a group merge
Facts worth recalling across sessions the auto-memory dir (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/)
Anything the repo should carry docs/ — committed

Write it durably as you go, not at the end. A restart gives no notice.

In a remote container, only a pushed commit is durable

The table above assumes a local machine, where .orchestrator/ outlives the Claude Code process. In Claude Code on the web the repository lives in an ephemeral container that is reclaimed after inactivity, and .orchestrator/ is gitignored — so it is destroyed with the container, and so is the auto-memory directory. /tmp and .orchestrator/ are equally volatile there.

So when the session is a remote container, the table collapses to one row: anything worth keeping goes into docs/ and is committed and pushed. Use .orchestrator/ for genuinely throwaway intermediates only, and promote anything a later session would want — findings, research, handoff notes — into committed documents before the work is done. docs/research/ and docs/handoffs/ exist for exactly this.

Plan digest (2026-09-23-001-refactor-review-loop-split-plan.md)

title: Split the review loop into responsibility modules with zero behaviour change type: refactor date: 2026-09-23 origin: docs/brainstorms/2026-09-21-unit-recipes-requirements.md (Plan A of its Next Step; direct description for the refactor itself)

Split the review loop into responsibility modules with zero behaviour change

Objective

orchestrator/execution/review.py (1,993 lines, 97 KB) is one class, _GroupExecution, that owns every responsibility a group's execution has: generation lifecycle, the coder↔reviewer round, session records and usage, the merge ladder, escalation and rewrite, surprises and prompt notes. The Unit Recipes brainstorm (R9 shared-plumbing) needs those responsibilities as separately importable pieces so a second executor can compose the ones it needs without inheriting the coder loop. This plan does exactly the split and nothing else: six modules, one composition root, every method body moved byte-for-byte, and the observable behaviour of a run identical. It is the "measurable beginning" the brainstorm names — the measure is the existing suite (1,935 tests on this branch, 104 s) passing with no test body changed, plus a layout test and a live-tier pass proving the new modules are real homes and the heartbeat still beats.

Not in scope: orchestrator/cli.py (3,258 lines) and sessions.py are left alone; no recipe, registry or dispatcher; no rename of review.py (that is Plan B's decision, when it becomes the code recipe's executor).

What we already know (resolved context)

The file and its public surface. orchestrator/execution/review.py exports, and is imported for, exactly these names (verified 2026-09-23 by grep over orchestrator/ and tests/):

name defined at imported by
MergeConflict review.py:119 execution/merge.py:21 (raises it), cli.py:97, tests/test_merge.py, tests/test_preflight.py, tests/test_review_loop.py
SurpriseBoard, surprise_residue, format_residue_report, REASON_* review.py:154–352 execution/finish.py:29, observatory/runs.py:30, cli.py:97, tests/test_finish.py, tests/test_surprise_board.py, tests/test_review_scratch.py, tests/test_review_loop.py
ReviewDeps, make_executor review.py:354, 397 cli.py:97 (single construction site at cli.py:2286), tests/test_review_loop.py, tests/test_review_scratch.py, tests/test_suspend_cure.py
GroupFailure not defined here — re-exported by accident from execution/scheduler.py tests/test_scheduler.py, tests/test_review_recovery_log.py, tests/test_merge_gate_triage.py, tests/test_review_loop.py
_GroupExecution review.py:406 tests/test_liveness_wiring.py
_spec_hash review.py:1963 tests/test_review_loop.py

Eleven test files and four package modules import from it. tests/test_review_loop.py (2,145 lines, 70 tests) is the main harness: it drives make_executor with a StubRunner and a Harness, and test_suspend_cure.py, test_liveness_wiring.py and test_merge_gate_triage.py import that harness.

The class's coupling map. A script over the method bodies (kept in the plan's Decisions rationale, not in the repo) shows which instance state each method touches. Shared state across responsibilities:

  • coder_entry, coder_sid, reviewer_sid: written in the generation body and _reenter, read by records, reviewer, merge (_resolve_conflict_in_place) and escalation (_resolve_needs_input).
  • handoff_prompt: set by _prepare_handoff (generation), _rewrite and _relaunch (escalation); consumed by the generation body.
  • sessions_spawned, rewrites: bumped by _record, _reenter, _rewrite, _relaunch; read by _breaker_reason.
  • _flake_reruns, _untracked_strikes: merge ladder only, reset per generation in the generation body.
  • _briefing_notes, _operator_notes, _env_failure, _grant_notes: the prompt-note channels; written by surprises/escalation/retire, read by the _apply_* helpers when the next prompt is built.
  • _current_round_no: written by _round_tag, read by _on_content_filtered.
  • _heartbeat, _cures, deps, ctx, group, gid, generation, workspace: constructed in __init__, read everywhere.

Every one of these is set in __init__ (review.py:409–478) or in the generation body; no method creates a new attribute later. That is what makes mixins over one self safe: the composition root's __init__ is the single place state is born.

Module-level helpers and their homes. _transcript_str (used by records lines 1066, 1086, 1921) → records.py. _short_test_summary (1422) and _move_paths (1361) → merge_ladder.py. _context_surprise (1673–1738), _is_retry (merge ladder and escalation, 8 sites) and _operator_surprise (merge ladder and escalation, 7 sites) → escalating.py (the existing execution/escalation.py is the broker and policy transport and keeps that name), imported by the merge ladder. _spec_hash (generation 635, re-entry 857, plus tests) → records.py. _ContentFilterStop is raised in _worker_call (522, 539) and caught in _run_generation (583, 591) → stays with generation.

What the executor seam looks like. Executor = Callable[[GroupContext], Awaitable[GroupState]] (execution/scheduler.py:281). make_executor(deps) returns a closure that constructs _GroupExecution(deps, ctx) and awaits .run(). The scheduler never sees the class. None of that changes.

merge.py imports review.py only for MergeConflict (merge.py:21); review.py does not import merge.py (the merge is injected as deps.merge_group). Moving MergeConflict into merge.py removes the only backward edge from the merge implementation into the loop, and creates no cycle: merge.py imports preflight, worktrees, config, model only.

Tooling. ruff is configured (pyproject.toml:35, line length 100, py312); no mypy section exists, so the host Protocol is checked by a test, not a type checker. Tests run with -m "not llm" by default (pyproject.toml:39); the live tier is -m llm and is driver-only in a worker sandbox. Baseline on this branch: 1935 passed, 22 deselected in 104.85s.

Documentation that names the file. docs/orchestrator-flow.md:52 ("review.py drives each group through coder/reviewer generations and rounds") and the orchestrator/execution/__init__.py docstring. The four docs/2026-08-*-findings.md files cite historical line numbers and are left as history.

Decisions

  • Mixins over the same self, plus a host Protocol. Each responsibility becomes a class with no __init__ in its own module; _GroupExecution inherits all six and keeps the only __init__. Every method body moves unchanged, so the diff is a move and reviewable as one. orchestrator/execution/host.py declares ExecutionHost, a typing.Protocol listing every attribute the composition root's __init__ sets (the list under coupling map above), and each mixin declares as class-level annotations the subset it reads — that is the seam Plan B's run executor satisfies. Rejected: composition with an explicit state object (every method line rewritten; regressions hide in the noise); a plain move with no protocol (the implicit state is exactly what a second executor cannot see).
  • Six modules by responsibility, one composition root. generation.py, reviewer.py, records.py, merge_ladder.py, escalating.py, surprises.py; review.py keeps ReviewDeps, make_executor, _GroupExecution.__init__, _current_child, _on_cure, _log. Rejected: three coarse modules (a run executor would import the coder loop to get session records).
  • No facade at the end; a transitional re-export during the moves. The end state: MergeConflict lives in execution/merge.py; SurpriseBoard and the residue helpers in execution/surprises.py; _spec_hash in execution/records.py; GroupFailure is imported from execution/scheduler.py, where it was always defined; review.py re-exports nothing it no longer defines, and the layout test asserts that from U7 on. During U1–U5 each moved public name keeps a one-line re-export in review.py marked # transitional re-export — removed in U7, so the eleven test files and four package importers are untouched while the bodies move, and each move's diff is the move alone. U6 switches the tests, U7 switches the package and deletes the re-exports. Test files change only their import statements. Rejected: switching importers in the same unit as each move (three units priced at 2–2.5× the cap because the estimator reads cli.py and tests/test_review_loop.py as full reads); a permanent facade (nothing outside the file would prove the new modules are the real homes, and it lingers).
  • The two importer units are priced far above their real work, and that is accepted. The estimator prices a file by its bytes, so an import-line edit to cli.py (138 KB) or the eleven test files (292 KB) prices as a full read: U6 and U7 show as over the cap in group --price. Their real work is a grep -n "from orchestrator.execution.review import" and an edit of that block per file; the unit prose says so and tells the worker not to open those files in full. group --no-spec accepts the plan (an over-cap single task is a cost flag, not a refusal); the retirement breaker is the backstop if a worker reads anyway.
  • Sequential units, one module per unit, each merged through Preflight before the next starts. Every unit rewrites review.py, so they cannot run in parallel; chaining them by depends_on makes each merge a full-suite checkpoint and keeps each worker's diff to one responsibility. Order is by coupling: surprises (module-level, almost no self), merge ladder, escalation handlers, records + reviewer, generation; then the two importer switches. Rejected: one unit for the whole split (one 97 KB file read plus six writes in one context, and one giant diff).
  • Two oracles beyond the suite. A layout test (tests/test_execution_layout.py) asserts the new modules' import graph is acyclic, that no two mixins define the same method name, that every attribute a mixin annotates is set by _GroupExecution.__init__, and that review.py defines none of the moved names. And the run driver executes the live tier (-m llm) after the last unit, because the risk this split exists to prevent — a second executor without heartbeat parity — is only visible with a real child.
  • cli.py is not split here. It is the next refactor candidate, but it has no bearing on R9, and the same "one file, one plan" discipline applies.

No ADR: the decisions are reversible file moves.

Unit summaries

  • U1 (surprises — SurpriseBoard, residue reporting and the prompt-note channel move to execution/surprises.py, with the host Protocol and the layout test that guard every later move) Summary: orchestrator/execution/surprises.py now owns SurpriseBoard, surprise_residue, format_residue_report, the REASON_* constants and a SurpriseHandling mixin (_spread, _handle_pending_surprises, _apply_briefing, _apply_env_notice, _apply_operator_note); orchestrator/execution/host.py declares the ExecutionHost Protocol every mixin annotates against; tests/test_execution_layout.py checks the layout mechanically; review.py keeps transitional re-exports of the moved public names until U7.
  • U2 (merge-ladder — the merge gate, untracked ladder, flake re-run and conflict resolution move to execution/merge_ladder.py; MergeConflict moves to execution/merge.py) Summary: orchestrator/execution/merge_ladder.py owns the MergeLadder mixin (_merge, _log_remerge, _should_rerun_for_flake, _handle_untracked, _archive_coder_scratch, _classify_preflight, _resolve_conflict_in_place, _log_driver_run_items, helpers _short_test_summary, _move_paths), and MergeConflict is defined in orchestrator/execution/merge.py, which no longer imports the loop; review.py re-exports MergeConflict transitionally.
  • U3 (escalating — escalation, approval gates, the coder-question channel, rewrite and relaunch move to execution/escalating.py) Summary: orchestrator/execution/escalating.py owns the EscalationHandlers mixin (_escalate, _approve_gate, _diff, _resolve_needs_input, _on_content_filtered, _on_coder_stuck, _on_reviewer_hard, _rewrite, _relaunch, _persist_rewritten_spec, _decisions_text, _advance_generation) and the helpers _context_surprise, _is_retry, _operator_surprise, which the merge ladder now imports from it; the existing execution/escalation.py (broker and policy transport) keeps its name and is not touched.
  • U4 (records-and-reviewer — session records, usage and transcript bookkeeping move to execution/records.py; the reviewer round moves to execution/reviewer.py) Summary: orchestrator/execution/records.py owns the SessionRecords mixin (_record, _copy_usage, _persist_coder_usage, _persist_reviewer_usage, _make_coder_on_turn, _adopt_actual_session_id, _refresh_transcript, _watch_transcript, _round_tag, _log_coder_session_end) plus _transcript_str and _spec_hash; orchestrator/execution/reviewer.py owns the ReviewerRound mixin (_review_round, _archive_review_scratch); review.py re-exports _spec_hash transitionally.
  • U5 (generation — the generation lifecycle moves to execution/generation.py, review.py becomes the composition root, and the docs describe the layout) Summary: orchestrator/execution/generation.py owns the GenerationLoop mixin (run, _run_generation, _run_generation_body, _find_reentry_session, _reenter, _launch_call, _reentry_fallback, _worker_call, _breaker_reason, _retire, _prepare_handoff, and _ContentFilterStop); orchestrator/execution/review.py is left with ReviewDeps, make_executor, the transitional re-exports, and _GroupExecution composed of the six mixins with only __init__, _current_child, _on_cure and _log; docs/orchestrator-flow.md and the execution/__init__.py docstring describe the layout.
  • U6 (test-importers — the eleven test files import every moved name from its new home, touching import statements only) Summary: The eleven test files that imported from orchestrator/execution/review.py now import SurpriseBoard, surprise_residue, format_residue_report and REASON_* from execution/surprises.py, MergeConflict from execution/merge.py, _spec_hash from execution/records.py, and GroupFailure from execution/scheduler.py; only import statements change.
  • U7 (package-importers — cli.py, finish.py, observatory/runs.py import from the new homes, the transitional re-exports are deleted, and the live tier proves nothing changed) Summary: orchestrator/cli.py, orchestrator/execution/finish.py and orchestrator/observatory/runs.py import the moved names from execution/surprises.py and execution/merge.py; review.py drops every # transitional re-export line and the layout test now asserts it defines none of the moved names; the run driver executes the live tier as the final oracle.

Implements / Consumes registry

10static annotations, and importing the concrete types at runtime would create

154class SurpriseBoard:
155 """Cross-group surprise registry. A mark is consumed by the named group's
156 executor at its next checkpoint (before launch, or before accepting an
157 approval); marks for completed/failed groups are simply never read.
158
159 Persisted to the run directory when constructed with ``paths`` (plan U7):
160 a plain in-memory dict dies with the process, silently dropping a surprise
161 marked for a group that has not yet run. ``paths=None`` keeps every
162 existing in-process test byte-identical.
163
164 ``groups`` (plan U11) is the run's real group list, used to validate every
165 id in a surprise's ``affected_groups``: a task id is resolved to its owning
166 group, and an id naming neither a group nor a task falls through to the
167 run-level bucket (key ``RUN_LEVEL``) instead of a dead bucket nothing ever
168 reads. ``groups=None`` (every existing caller before this unit) skips
169 validation entirely, so ids like the tests' bare "g0"/"g3" keep working
170 unchanged.
171 """
172
173 #: Bucket key for a surprise whose id names neither a real group nor a task
174 #: owned by one — otherwise silently dropped, per plan U11.
175 RUN_LEVEL = "__run__"
176
177 def __init__(self, paths: RunPaths | None = None, *, groups: list[Group] | None = None) -> None:
178 self._paths = paths
179 self._lock = threading.Lock()
180 self._pending: dict[str, list[Surprise]] = {}
181 self._group_ids: frozenset[str] | None = (
182 frozenset(g.id for g in groups) if groups is not None else None
183 )
184 self._task_owner: dict[str, str] = {}
185 # Case-folded full task ids and their leading token ("u8" for
186 # "u8-structure-fix-budget"): workers name tasks the way the plan does
187 # ("U8"), not by the slugged id the grouper assigned.
188 self._task_alias_owner: dict[str, str] = {}
189 if groups is not None:
190 for group in groups:
191 for task in group.tasks:
192 self._task_owner.setdefault(task, group.id)
193 self._task_alias_owner.setdefault(task.lower(), group.id)
194 head = task.split("-", 1)[0].lower()
195 if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in head):
196 self._task_alias_owner.setdefault(head, group.id)
197 if paths is not None and paths.surprises_path.is_file():
198 raw = json.loads(paths.surprises_path.read_text())
199 self._pending = {
200 gid: [Surprise.model_validate(item) for item in items] for gid, items in raw.items()
201 }
202
203 def mark(self, surprise: Surprise, *, source_group: str | None = None) -> None:
204 with self._lock:
205 targets = [gid for gid in surprise.affected_groups if gid != source_group]
206 if len(targets) > WIDE_FANOUT_THRESHOLD:
207 _logger.warning(
208 "surprise from %s names %d groups (wide fan-out): %s",
209 source_group,
210 len(targets),
211 surprise.description,
212 )
213 keys: list[str] = []
214 for gid in targets:
215 for key in self._resolve(gid, surprise, source_group):
216 if key not in keys:
217 keys.append(key)
218 if not keys and self._group_ids is not None:
219 # No other group named (an empty list, or only the source
220 # itself): a finding about future work, which must reach the
221 # run's residue report rather than vanish.
222 keys.append(self.RUN_LEVEL)
223 for key in keys:
224 self._append(key, surprise)
225 self._persist()
226
227 def _resolve(self, gid: str, surprise: Surprise, source_group: str | None) -> list[str]:
228 """Map a raw ``affected_groups`` id to the buckets it should land in."""
229 if self._group_ids is None:
230 return [gid] # no group list configured — legacy, unvalidated behavior
231 if gid in self._group_ids:
232 return [gid]
233 owner = self._task_owner.get(gid)
234 if owner is not None:
235 return [owner]
236 # A decorated id — "g3 (structure-fix-budget/U8)" in r20260908. Plan
237 # task ids are what a worker actually knows, so a task token wins over
238 # a group token that may be a guess.
239 tokens = [t.lower() for t in _ID_TOKEN.findall(gid)]
240 task_owners = [self._task_alias_owner[t] for t in tokens if t in self._task_alias_owner]
241 group_hits = [t for t in tokens if t in self._group_ids]
242 resolved = list(dict.fromkeys(task_owners or group_hits))
243 if resolved:
244 _logger.info(
245 "surprise from %s names %r — resolved to %s", source_group, gid, ", ".join(resolved)
246 )
247 return resolved
248 _logger.warning(
249 "surprise from %s names unknown id %s (no matching group or task): %s",
250 source_group,
251 gid,
252 surprise.description,
253 )
254 return [self.RUN_LEVEL]
255
256 def _append(self, key: str, surprise: Surprise) -> None:
257 """Append, deduplicating an identical surprise already pending in this
258 bucket (plan U11): successive rounds/generations re-emit the same
259 finding, and a dead-simple in-list check is enough since a bucket
260 rarely holds more than a handful of entries."""
261 bucket = self._pending.setdefault(key, [])
262 if surprise not in bucket:
263 bucket.append(surprise)
264
265 def pending_for(self, group_id: str) -> list[Surprise]:
266 with self._lock:
267 return list(self._pending.get(group_id, []))
268
269 def consume(self, group_id: str) -> list[Surprise]:
270 with self._lock:
271 surprises = self._pending.pop(group_id, [])
272 if surprises:
273 self._persist()
274 return surprises
275
276 def _persist(self) -> None:
277 if self._paths is None:
278 return
279 payload = {
280 gid: [surprise.model_dump() for surprise in surprises]
281 for gid, surprises in self._pending.items()
282 }
283 atomic_write_text(self._paths.surprises_path, json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
284

286#: Reason strings for a residue entry (plan U12) — a bucket resolved to a real
287#: group whose state is terminal-completed never gets another checkpoint to
288#: consume it at; ``RUN_LEVEL`` never named a group at all; anything else was
289#: still reachable when the run stopped.
290REASON_GROUP_COMPLETED = "never delivered — group already completed"
291REASON_UNKNOWN_GROUP = "unknown group id"
292REASON_RUN_ENDED = "run ended before delivery"
293

295def surprise_residue(paths: RunPaths, state: RunState | None) -> list[SurpriseResidueEntry]:
296 """Every bucket still on the board when the run ended, each labelled with
297 why (plan U12). Reads ``surprises.json`` directly rather than constructing
298 a ``SurpriseBoard`` — a residue report has no group list to validate
299 against and must never mutate the file it is reporting on. Sorted by
300 bucket for a stable, readable listing.
301 """
302 if not paths.surprises_path.is_file():
303 return []
304 try:
305 raw = json.loads(paths.surprises_path.read_text())
306 except json.JSONDecodeError:
307 return []
308 entries: list[SurpriseResidueEntry] = []
309 for bucket, items in raw.items():
310 surprises = [Surprise.model_validate(item) for item in items]
311 if not surprises:
312 continue
313 entries.append(
314 SurpriseResidueEntry(
315 bucket=bucket,
316 count=len(surprises),
317 reason=_residue_reason(bucket, state),
318 surprises=surprises,
319 )
320 )
321 entries.sort(key=lambda entry: entry.bucket)
322 return entries
323
324
325def _residue_reason(bucket: str, state: RunState | None) -> str:
326 if bucket == SurpriseBoard.RUN_LEVEL:
327 return REASON_UNKNOWN_GROUP
328 group_state = state.groups.get(bucket) if state is not None else None
329 if group_state is not None and group_state.state in (
330 GroupState.COMPLETED,
331 GroupState.RESOLVED,
332 ):
333 return REASON_GROUP_COMPLETED
334 return REASON_RUN_ENDED
335
336
337def format_residue_report(entries: list[SurpriseResidueEntry]) -> str:
338 """Human-readable rendering shared by the CLI end-of-run summary and
339 `finish` (plan U12). An empty board renders an explicit "none pending"
340 rather than a bare heading — the whole point is that the operator should
341 never have to open ``surprises.json`` to learn the board is empty."""
342 lines = ["surprises pending at end of run:"]
343 if not entries:
344 lines.append(" none pending")
345 return "\n".join(lines)
346 for entry in entries:
347 lines.append(f" {entry.bucket}: {entry.count} pending — {entry.reason}")
348 for surprise in entry.surprises:
349 lines.append(f" - [{surprise.kind}] {surprise.description}")
350 return "\n".join(lines)

orchestrator/execution/surprises.py
@@ -0,0 +1,332 @@
1"""Cross-group surprise registry, its residue reporting, and the per-group
2prompt-note channels that consume it (plan U1 of the review-loop split).
3
4Surprises fan out through the `SurpriseBoard`: unfinished groups named by a
5surprise are rewritten before launch — or instead of merging, when already in
6review (origin R12, R16). Completed groups are never rewritten. `surprise_residue`
7and `format_residue_report` report on whatever the board never delivered by
8the time a run ends.
9"""
10
11from __future__ import annotations
12
13import json
14import logging
15import re
16import threading
17from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
18from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
19
20from orchestrator.execution.manifest import RunPaths, atomic_write_text
21from orchestrator.execution.scheduler import GroupState, RunState
22from orchestrator.model import Group, Surprise, SurpriseResidueEntry
23
24if TYPE_CHECKING:
25 from orchestrator.execution.review import ReviewDeps
26
27_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
28
29#: Above this many named groups a mark is logged as a wide fan-out warning
30#: (plan U11 Decisions) — delivered in full regardless, never truncated: the
31#: informational kind (plan U13) is the real fix for a broad note draining
32#: rewrite budgets, so capping fan-out here would only bite a genuinely
33#: rewrite-worthy broadcast.
34WIDE_FANOUT_THRESHOLD = 5
35
36#: One id-like token inside a decorated ``affected_groups`` entry.
37_ID_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*")
38
39
40class SurpriseBoard:
41 """Cross-group surprise registry. A mark is consumed by the named group's
42 executor at its next checkpoint (before launch, or before accepting an
43 approval); marks for completed/failed groups are simply never read.
44
45 Persisted to the run directory when constructed with ``paths`` (plan U7):
46 a plain in-memory dict dies with the process, silently dropping a surprise
47 marked for a group that has not yet run. ``paths=None`` keeps every
48 existing in-process test byte-identical.
49
50 ``groups`` (plan U11) is the run's real group list, used to validate every
51 id in a surprise's ``affected_groups``: a task id is resolved to its owning
52 group, and an id naming neither a group nor a task falls through to the
53 run-level bucket (key ``RUN_LEVEL``) instead of a dead bucket nothing ever
54 reads. ``groups=None`` (every existing caller before this unit) skips
55 validation entirely, so ids like the tests' bare "g0"/"g3" keep working
56 unchanged.
57 """
58
59 #: Bucket key for a surprise whose id names neither a real group nor a task
60 #: owned by one — otherwise silently dropped, per plan U11.
61 RUN_LEVEL = "__run__"
62
63 def __init__(self, paths: RunPaths | None = None, *, groups: list[Group] | None = None) -> None:
64 self._paths = paths
65 self._lock = threading.Lock()
66 self._pending: dict[str, list[Surprise]] = {}
67 self._group_ids: frozenset[str] | None = (
68 frozenset(g.id for g in groups) if groups is not None else None
69 )
70 self._task_owner: dict[str, str] = {}
71 # Case-folded full task ids and their leading token ("u8" for
72 # "u8-structure-fix-budget"): workers name tasks the way the plan does
73 # ("U8"), not by the slugged id the grouper assigned.
74 self._task_alias_owner: dict[str, str] = {}
75 if groups is not None:
76 for group in groups:
77 for task in group.tasks:
78 self._task_owner.setdefault(task, group.id)
79 self._task_alias_owner.setdefault(task.lower(), group.id)
80 head = task.split("-", 1)[0].lower()
81 if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in head):
82 self._task_alias_owner.setdefault(head, group.id)
83 if paths is not None and paths.surprises_path.is_file():
84 raw = json.loads(paths.surprises_path.read_text())
85 self._pending = {
86 gid: [Surprise.model_validate(item) for item in items] for gid, items in raw.items()
87 }
88
89 def mark(self, surprise: Surprise, *, source_group: str | None = None) -> None:
90 with self._lock:
91 targets = [gid for gid in surprise.affected_groups if gid != source_group]
92 if len(targets) > WIDE_FANOUT_THRESHOLD:
93 _logger.warning(
94 "surprise from %s names %d groups (wide fan-out): %s",
95 source_group,
96 len(targets),
97 surprise.description,
98 )
99 keys: list[str] = []
100 for gid in targets:
101 for key in self._resolve(gid, surprise, source_group):
102 if key not in keys:
103 keys.append(key)
104 if not keys and self._group_ids is not None:
105 # No other group named (an empty list, or only the source
106 # itself): a finding about future work, which must reach the
107 # run's residue report rather than vanish.
108 keys.append(self.RUN_LEVEL)
109 for key in keys:
110 self._append(key, surprise)
111 self._persist()
112
113 def _resolve(self, gid: str, surprise: Surprise, source_group: str | None) -> list[str]:
114 """Map a raw ``affected_groups`` id to the buckets it should land in."""
115 if self._group_ids is None:
116 return [gid] # no group list configured — legacy, unvalidated behavior
117 if gid in self._group_ids:
118 return [gid]
119 owner = self._task_owner.get(gid)
120 if owner is not None:
121 return [owner]
122 # A decorated id — "g3 (structure-fix-budget/U8)" in r20260908. Plan
123 # task ids are what a worker actually knows, so a task token wins over
124 # a group token that may be a guess.
125 tokens = [t.lower() for t in _ID_TOKEN.findall(gid)]
126 task_owners = [self._task_alias_owner[t] for t in tokens if t in self._task_alias_owner]
127 group_hits = [t for t in tokens if t in self._group_ids]
128 resolved = list(dict.fromkeys(task_owners or group_hits))
129 if resolved:
130 _logger.info(
131 "surprise from %s names %r — resolved to %s", source_group, gid, ", ".join(resolved)
132 )
133 return resolved
134 _logger.warning(
135 "surprise from %s names unknown id %s (no matching group or task): %s",
136 source_group,
137 gid,
138 surprise.description,
139 )
140 return [self.RUN_LEVEL]
141
142 def _append(self, key: str, surprise: Surprise) -> None:
143 """Append, deduplicating an identical surprise already pending in this
144 bucket (plan U11): successive rounds/generations re-emit the same
145 finding, and a dead-simple in-list check is enough since a bucket
146 rarely holds more than a handful of entries."""
147 bucket = self._pending.setdefault(key, [])
148 if surprise not in bucket:
149 bucket.append(surprise)
150
151 def pending_for(self, group_id: str) -> list[Surprise]:
152 with self._lock:
153 return list(self._pending.get(group_id, []))
154
155 def consume(self, group_id: str) -> list[Surprise]:
156 with self._lock:
157 surprises = self._pending.pop(group_id, [])
158 if surprises:
159 self._persist()
160 return surprises
161
162 def _persist(self) -> None:
163 if self._paths is None:
164 return
165 payload = {
166 gid: [surprise.model_dump() for surprise in surprises]
167 for gid, surprises in self._pending.items()
168 }
169 atomic_write_text(self._paths.surprises_path, json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
170
171
172#: Reason strings for a residue entry (plan U12) — a bucket resolved to a real
173#: group whose state is terminal-completed never gets another checkpoint to
174#: consume it at; ``RUN_LEVEL`` never named a group at all; anything else was
175#: still reachable when the run stopped.
176REASON_GROUP_COMPLETED = "never delivered — group already completed"
177REASON_UNKNOWN_GROUP = "unknown group id"
178REASON_RUN_ENDED = "run ended before delivery"
179
180
181def surprise_residue(paths: RunPaths, state: RunState | None) -> list[SurpriseResidueEntry]:
182 """Every bucket still on the board when the run ended, each labelled with
183 why (plan U12). Reads ``surprises.json`` directly rather than constructing
184 a ``SurpriseBoard`` — a residue report has no group list to validate
185 against and must never mutate the file it is reporting on. Sorted by
186 bucket for a stable, readable listing.
187 """
188 if not paths.surprises_path.is_file():
189 return []
190 try:
191 raw = json.loads(paths.surprises_path.read_text())
192 except json.JSONDecodeError:
193 return []
194 entries: list[SurpriseResidueEntry] = []
195 for bucket, items in raw.items():
196 surprises = [Surprise.model_validate(item) for item in items]
197 if not surprises:
198 continue
199 entries.append(
200 SurpriseResidueEntry(
201 bucket=bucket,
202 count=len(surprises),
203 reason=_residue_reason(bucket, state),
204 surprises=surprises,
205 )
206 )
207 entries.sort(key=lambda entry: entry.bucket)
208 return entries
209
210
211def _residue_reason(bucket: str, state: RunState | None) -> str:
212 if bucket == SurpriseBoard.RUN_LEVEL:
213 return REASON_UNKNOWN_GROUP
214 group_state = state.groups.get(bucket) if state is not None else None
215 if group_state is not None and group_state.state in (
216 GroupState.COMPLETED,
217 GroupState.RESOLVED,
218 ):
219 return REASON_GROUP_COMPLETED
220 return REASON_RUN_ENDED
221
222
223def format_residue_report(entries: list[SurpriseResidueEntry]) -> str:
224 """Human-readable rendering shared by the CLI end-of-run summary and
225 `finish` (plan U12). An empty board renders an explicit "none pending"
226 rather than a bare heading — the whole point is that the operator should
227 never have to open ``surprises.json`` to learn the board is empty."""
228 lines = ["surprises pending at end of run:"]
229 if not entries:
230 lines.append(" none pending")
231 return "\n".join(lines)
232 for entry in entries:
233 lines.append(f" {entry.bucket}: {entry.count} pending — {entry.reason}")
234 for surprise in entry.surprises:
235 lines.append(f" - [{surprise.kind}] {surprise.description}")
236 return "\n".join(lines)
237
238
239class SurpriseHandling:
240 """The surprise board's consumer side and the three prompt-note channels
241 a group's coder prompt is built from: informational surprise briefings,
242 an environment-provisioning notice, and an operator's `retry` note. Mixed
243 onto `_GroupExecution`, whose `__init__` is the only place the attributes
244 below are born (see `ExecutionHost`)."""
245
246 gid: str
247 group: Group
248 deps: ReviewDeps
249 _briefing_notes: list[str]
250 _operator_notes: list[str]
251 _env_failure: str | None
252 _log: Callable[[str], None]
253 _rewrite: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]
254
255 def _spread(self, surprises: list[Surprise]) -> None:
256 """Fan surprises out to the groups they name — never back at the source."""
257 for surprise in surprises:
258 self.deps.board.mark(surprise, source_group=self.gid)
259
260 async def _handle_pending_surprises(self, reason: str) -> bool:
261 """Consume this group's pending surprises at a checkpoint (before
262 launch, or before an approval is accepted). A surprise whose kind is
263 anything but ``informational`` is rewrite-worthy: any such surprise
264 pending triggers a full rewrite (spec + speccer call, one rewrite
265 spent), which also consumes every other pending surprise including any
266 informational ones mixed in. When only informational surprises are
267 pending, they cost nothing: consumed here and folded into the next
268 prompt this generation builds (plan U13), never touching
269 ``rewrite_spec`` or the rewrite counter.
270
271 Returns True when a rewrite happened, so the caller can bail out of its
272 current path (merge/approval) the way it always has.
273 """
274 pending = self.deps.board.pending_for(self.gid)
275 if not pending:
276 return False
277 if any(surprise.kind != "informational" for surprise in pending):
278 await self._rewrite(reason)
279 return True
280 informational = self.deps.board.consume(self.gid)
281 self._briefing_notes.extend(surprise.description for surprise in informational)
282 self._log(
283 f"group {self.gid}: {len(informational)} informational surprise(s) "
284 "folded into the next briefing (no rewrite spent)"
285 )
286 return False
287
288 def _apply_briefing(self, prompt: str) -> str:
289 """Fold any consumed informational surprises into a coder prompt about
290 to be sent (plan U13), then clear them — a one-shot addition to
291 whichever prompt this generation happens to build next (a fresh
292 launch, or a breaker handoff)."""
293 if not self._briefing_notes:
294 return prompt
295 notes = "\n".join(f"- {note}" for note in self._briefing_notes)
296 self._briefing_notes = []
297 return f"{prompt}\n\n## Informational updates from other groups\n{notes}\n"
298
299 def _apply_env_notice(self, prompt: str) -> str:
300 """Tell a coder whose worktree failed to provision (warn mode) exactly
301 what failed, once. Silent completion with a green self-verification
302 against a missing environment is the worst of the three outcomes;
303 this is the least the worker must know to avoid it."""
304 if not self._env_failure:
305 return prompt
306 notice = self._env_failure
307 self._env_failure = None
308 return (
309 f"{prompt}\n\n## Environment warning\n"
310 "Provisioning this worktree's environment FAILED before you started, "
311 "so nothing here has a working venv yet:\n\n```\n"
312 f"{notice}\n```\n\n"
313 "Fix the dependency spec if the cause is in this repo, re-run `uv sync` "
314 "in the worktree, and do not report any verification item as passed "
315 "unless it ran in a working environment. If you cannot repair the "
316 "environment, report status `blocked` and say so.\n"
317 )
318
319 def _apply_operator_note(self, prompt: str) -> str:
320 """Fold an operator's ``retry`` note into the coder prompt about to be
321 sent, once: what was fixed outside the worker and why it should go again
322 on the unchanged spec."""
323 if not self._operator_notes:
324 return prompt
325 notes = "\n".join(f"- {note}" for note in self._operator_notes)
326 self._operator_notes = []
327 return (
328 f"{prompt}\n\n## Operator note\n"
329 "The previous attempt at this spec stopped; the operator fixed the cause "
330 "outside your session and relaunched you on the same spec:\n"
331 f"{notes}\n"
332 )
tests/test_execution_layout.py
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
1"""Layout guard for the review-loop split (plan U1 and on).
2
3Every later unit adds a mixin to `_GroupExecution`; this test is the
4mechanical check every one of them must keep passing: the new modules import
5without a cycle, each mixin's declared reads exist on the host, every host
6attribute the mixins rely on is actually set by `_GroupExecution.__init__`,
7and no two mixins in the MRO define the same method (a silent override would
8mean one of them dead code).
9"""
10
11from __future__ import annotations
12
13import subprocess
14import sys
15from pathlib import Path
16
17from orchestrator.execution.host import ExecutionHost
18from orchestrator.execution.review import _GroupExecution
19from orchestrator.execution.surprises import SurpriseHandling
20from tests.test_review_loop import Harness, StubRunner, make_group
21
22MIXINS = [SurpriseHandling]
23
24
25def test_new_modules_import_with_no_cycle():
26 """Each module imports cleanly on its own, in either order — a real cycle
27 would raise ImportError/AttributeError on a partially-initialized module."""
28 for order in (
29 [
30 "orchestrator.execution.host",
31 "orchestrator.execution.surprises",
32 "orchestrator.execution.review",
33 ],
34 [
35 "orchestrator.execution.review",
36 "orchestrator.execution.surprises",
37 "orchestrator.execution.host",
38 ],
39 ):
40 script = "; ".join(f"import {name}" for name in order)
41 result = subprocess.run(
42 [sys.executable, "-c", script],
43 cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1],
44 capture_output=True,
45 text=True,
46 )
47 assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
48
49
50def test_mixin_annotations_name_a_host_attribute_or_method():
51 # Raw annotation names only — not resolved types: `ExecutionHost`'s
52 # annotations reference types imported under `TYPE_CHECKING`, which are
53 # absent from the module's runtime globals, so `get_type_hints` would
54 # raise trying to evaluate the (stringified, PEP 563) forward refs.
55 host_hints = set(ExecutionHost.__annotations__)
56 for mixin in MIXINS:
57 mixin_annotations = getattr(mixin, "__annotations__", {})
58 for name in mixin_annotations:
59 assert name in host_hints or hasattr(ExecutionHost, name), (
60 f"{mixin.__name__}.{name} names neither an ExecutionHost data "
61 f"attribute nor an ExecutionHost method"
62 )
63
64
65def test_every_host_attribute_is_set_by_group_execution_init(tmp_path):
66 runner = StubRunner({})
67 harness = Harness(tmp_path, runner)
68 group = make_group()
69 ctx = harness.context(group)
70 execution = _GroupExecution(harness.deps, ctx)
71 instance_vars = vars(execution)
72 for name in ExecutionHost.__annotations__:
73 assert name in instance_vars, f"ExecutionHost.{name} is never assigned in __init__"
74
75
76def test_no_method_name_collides_across_mixins():
77 seen: dict[str, type] = {}
78 for mixin in MIXINS:
79 for name, value in vars(mixin).items():
80 if name.startswith("__") or not callable(value):
81 continue
82 if name in seen and seen[name] is not mixin:
83 raise AssertionError(
84 f"{name} is defined on both {seen[name].__name__} and {mixin.__name__}"
85 )
86 seen[name] = mixin
87
88
89def test_review_module_reexports_are_the_documented_transitional_set():
90 """Guards the U7 cleanup: these are exactly the names review.py must stop
91 defining once every unit has moved its piece out."""
92 import orchestrator.execution.review as review
93
94 for name in (
95 "SurpriseBoard",
96 "SurpriseHandling",
97 "surprise_residue",
98 "format_residue_report",
99 "REASON_GROUP_COMPLETED",
100 "REASON_UNKNOWN_GROUP",
101 "REASON_RUN_ENDED",
102 ):
103 assert hasattr(review, name)

Plan section U2

U2. merge-ladder — the merge gate, untracked ladder, flake re-run and conflict resolution move to execution/merge_ladder.py; MergeConflict moves to execution/merge.py

  • Summary: orchestrator/execution/merge_ladder.py owns the MergeLadder mixin (_merge, _log_remerge, _should_rerun_for_flake, _handle_untracked, _archive_coder_scratch, _classify_preflight, _resolve_conflict_in_place, _log_driver_run_items, helpers _short_test_summary, _move_paths), and MergeConflict is defined in orchestrator/execution/merge.py, which no longer imports the loop; review.py re-exports MergeConflict transitionally.

MergeLadder annotates the host attributes it reads (deps, ctx, group, gid, generation, workspace, coder_sid, coder_entry, _flake_reruns, _untracked_strikes, _heartbeat, _log, _escalate, _rewrite, _relaunch, _spread, _persist_coder_usage, _make_coder_on_turn). _is_retry and _operator_surprise are still imported from review.py in this unit (they move with the escalation handlers in U3).

1"""The merge gate and everything that fires when it fails: the untracked
2ladder, the one-shot flake re-run, preflight classification and in-place
3conflict resolution (plan U2 of the review-loop split).
4
5`MergeLadder` is mixed onto `_GroupExecution`, whose `__init__` is the only
6place the attributes below are born (see `ExecutionHost`).
7"""

46class MergeLadder:
47 """Merge gate, untracked ladder, flake re-run and conflict resolution."""
48

50 ctx: GroupContext
51 group: Group
52 gid: str
53 generation: int
54 workspace: Path | None

56 coder_entry: SessionEntry | None
57 _flake_reruns: int
58 _untracked_strikes: int
59 _heartbeat: RoundHeartbeat

68 def _log_driver_run_items(self) -> None:
69 """Name the items the coder was told not to run, once, at merge.
70
71 A `driver_run` item passes the verification gate untouched (see
72 `unmet_required_verification`), so without this line the only trace
73 of an unrun check would be a `skipped` result buried in the report.
74 The driver reads this line and runs them before `finish`.
75 """
76 pending = [item.id for item in self.group.verification if item.driver_run]
77 if pending:
78 self._log(
79 f"group {self.gid}: {len(pending)} driver-run verification item(s) "
80 f"not run by the coder — {', '.join(pending)}"
81 )
82
83 async def _merge(self) -> bool:
84 assert self.workspace is not None
85 attempts_left = self.deps.execution.max_conflict_resolve_attempts
86 while True:
87 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.MERGING)
88 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("merging into integration") # F4
89 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: merge attempt")
90 self._archive_coder_scratch()
91 try:
92 await asyncio.to_thread(self.deps.merge_group, self.group, self.workspace)
93 except MergeConflict as exc:
94 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: merge conflict ({exc})")
95 conflict = Surprise(
96 kind="merge_conflict", description=str(exc), affected_groups=exc.affected_groups
97 )
98 self._spread([conflict])
99 if attempts_left > 0:
100 attempts_left -= 1
101 if await self._resolve_conflict_in_place(exc):
102 continue # retry the merge with the resolved worktree
103 response = await self._escalate(
104 EscalationKind.MERGE_CONFLICT,
105 prompt=f"merge conflict for {self.gid}: {exc}",
106 surprises=[conflict],
107 )
108 # An operator `retry` here means the same as `answer`: the text
109 # guides the rewrite (a conflict is evidence about the diff).
110 extra = [conflict]
111 if response is not None:
112 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
113 await self._rewrite(f"merge conflict: {exc}", extra=extra)
114 return False
115 except PreflightFailure as exc:
116 # Not a git conflict — no coder resume is attempted in place
117 # (plan U4 Decisions: only a concrete git/test failure ever
118 # warrants an LLM call, and the in-place resume is specific to
119 # resolving conflict markers).
120 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: preflight failed ({exc})")
121 if exc.kind == "untracked":
122 if await self._handle_untracked(exc):
123 continue # the tree was cleaned in place: re-run the gate
124 return False # relaunched on the same spec
125 diagnosis, attributable = self._classify_preflight(exc)
126 surprise = Surprise(kind="other", description=diagnosis, affected_groups=[self.gid])
127 self._spread([surprise])
128 if attributable:
129 if self._should_rerun_for_flake(exc):
130 self._flake_reruns += 1
131 self._log(
132 f"group {self.gid}: preflight: re-running gate once (suspected flake)"
133 )
134 continue
135 # A new, real regression — escalate, then rewrite (plan U3):
136 # the failure is evidence about the diff and a rewritten
137 # spec can act on it.
138 response = await self._escalate(
139 EscalationKind.PREFLIGHT_FAILED,
140 prompt=f"preflight failed for {self.gid}: {exc}",
141 surprises=[surprise],
142 )
143 if _is_retry(response):
144 if not response.answer.strip():
145 # The operator fixed the world by hand and the tree
146 # is unchanged: re-run the gate, no LLM call.
147 self._log_remerge("operator retry with no text")
148 continue
149 # With text: the operator changed something the coder
150 # must know about (a test, a fixture) — same spec,
151 # fresh coder, the text as its briefing.
152 await self._relaunch(response.answer, f"preflight failed: {exc}")
153 return False
154 extra = [surprise]
155 if response is not None:
156 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
157 await self._rewrite(f"preflight failed: {exc}", extra=extra)
158 return False
159 # env/timeout, or every failing test was already red on the
160 # launch branch: not evidence about the diff, so no rewrite is
161 # spent on it (plan U3 Decisions) — escalate for visibility only,
162 # the group fails fast either way.
163 response = await self._escalate(
164 EscalationKind.PREFLIGHT_FAILED,
165 prompt=f"preflight failed for {self.gid} (not attributable to this diff): {exc}",
166 surprises=[surprise],
167 )
168 if _is_retry(response) and not response.answer.strip():
169 self._log_remerge("operator retry with no text")
170 continue
171 if response is not None:
172 diagnosis += f"\n[operator] {response.answer}"
173 raise GroupFailure(diagnosis) from exc
174 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: merged into the integration branch")
175 self._log_driver_run_items()
176 return True
177
178 def _log_remerge(self, reason: str) -> None:
179 """The cheap ``preflight_failed`` resolution: refresh + preflight + merge
180 again with no LLM call — the caller ``continue``s the merge loop."""
181 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: re-running the merge gate ({reason})")
182
183 def _should_rerun_for_flake(self, exc: PreflightFailure) -> bool:
184 """One automatic re-run of the gate on an attributable regression when
185 nobody is there to `retry` by hand (autonomous for this kind), so a
186 flaky test does not cost a rewrite plus a coder generation. Capped at
187 one per generation: a second identical failure is a real regression."""
188 if exc.kind != "regression" or self._flake_reruns >= 1:
189 return False
190 policy, broker = self.deps.policy, self.deps.broker
191 autonomous = broker is None or policy is None
192 autonomous = autonomous or not policy.should_escalate(EscalationKind.PREFLIGHT_FAILED)
193 return autonomous
194
195 async def _handle_untracked(self, exc: PreflightFailure) -> bool:
196 """The untracked ladder. Returns True when the gate should simply be
197 re-run (the tree was cleaned in place, by the operator or by archiving),
198 False when a fresh coder was relaunched on the same spec.
199
200 First strike: attributable to the coder, but cheap — no rewrite, no
201 speccer; a same-spec relaunch carrying an operator note that names the
202 paths. Second consecutive strike: the leftovers are moved to the
203 group's ``untracked/`` archive, a surprise records it for the report,
204 and the merge proceeds.
205 """
206 assert self.workspace is not None
207 self._untracked_strikes += 1
208 paths = ", ".join(exc.paths)
209 note = (
210 f"untracked files left in the worktree: {paths} — commit them, move them "
211 f"into {CODER_SCRATCH_DIRNAME}/, or delete them"
212 )
213 if self._untracked_strikes >= 2:
214 archive = self.deps.store.paths.untracked_archive_dir(self.gid)
215 _move_paths(self.workspace, exc.paths, archive)
216 self._log(
217 f"group {self.gid}: UNTRACKED FILES ARCHIVED after a second consecutive "
218 f"untracked-only gate failure — moved to {archive}: {paths}; merging anyway"
219 )
220 self._spread(
221 [
222 Surprise(
223 kind="informational",
224 description=(
225 f"group {self.gid} left untracked files twice; archived to "
226 f"{archive} and merged without them: {paths}"
227 ),
228 affected_groups=[self.gid],
229 )
230 ]
231 )
232 self._log_remerge("untracked leftovers archived")
233 return True
234 response = await self._escalate(
235 EscalationKind.PREFLIGHT_FAILED,
236 prompt=f"preflight failed for {self.gid} (untracked files): {exc}",
237 )
238 if _is_retry(response) and not response.answer.strip():
239 self._log_remerge("operator retry with no text")
240 return True
241 if response is not None and response.answer.strip():
242 note = f"{note}\n[operator] {response.answer}"
243 await self._relaunch(note, f"untracked files left in the worktree: {paths}")
244 return False
245
246 def _archive_coder_scratch(self) -> None:
247 """Exclude and archive the coder's scratch directory before the gate
248 runs, mirroring ``_archive_review_scratch`` — same cap, archived beside
249 the group's artifacts. A no-op when it was never created."""
250 assert self.workspace is not None
251 scratch_dir = self.workspace / CODER_SCRATCH_DIRNAME
252 if not scratch_dir.exists():
253 return
254 ensure_excluded(self.workspace, CODER_SCRATCH_DIRNAME)
255 archive_review_scratch(
256 scratch_dir,
257 self.deps.store.paths.coder_scratch_archive_dir(self.gid),
258 cap_bytes=self.deps.execution.review_scratch_cap_bytes,
259 log=self._log,
260 )

262 def _classify_preflight(self, exc: PreflightFailure) -> tuple[str, bool]:
263 """Route a preflight failure by cause (plan U3): ``env``/``timeout``
264 never ran a real test, and a ``regression`` whose failing tests are all
265 already red on the launch branch is not evidence about this diff
266 either — neither is attributable, and the caller must not spend a
267 rewrite on it. Only a genuinely new, run failure is attributable.
268
269 Returns the diagnosis text handed to the next generation (or the
270 operator) — carrying the check output's own "short test summary info"
271 tail, not just a path to the log — and whether the failure is
272 attributable.
273 """
274 summary_tail = ""
275 if exc.output_path is not None and exc.output_path.is_file():
276 summary_tail = _short_test_summary(exc.output_path.read_text())
277 if exc.kind in ("env", "timeout", "untracked"):
278 diagnosis = f"preflight failed ({exc.kind}): {exc.reason}"
279 if summary_tail:
280 diagnosis += f"\n{summary_tail}"
281 return diagnosis, False
282 # kind == "regression": tests actually ran and something actually
283 # failed — the only question left is whether it is new. The gate
284 # already answered that (it had to, to decide whether to raise), so
285 # take its verdict rather than re-deriving one: re-derivation guessed a
286 # single `preflight-junit.xml` beside the log and so was blind to the
287 # UI steps' own reports. The fallback covers a `PreflightFailure`
288 # raised from somewhere other than `run_preflight`.
289 comparison = exc.comparison
290 if comparison is None:
291 junit_path = (
292 exc.output_path.parent / "preflight-junit.xml"
293 if exc.output_path is not None
294 else None
295 )
296 failing = (
297 failing_tests_from_junit(junit_path) if junit_path is not None else frozenset()
298 )
299 comparison = compare_to_baseline(self.deps.preflight_baseline, failing)
300 if comparison.verdict == "pre_existing":
301 diagnosis = (
302 f"preflight failed (pre-existing): {exc.reason} — every failing test was "
303 "already failing on the launch branch"
304 )
305 if summary_tail:
306 diagnosis += f"\n{summary_tail}"
307 return diagnosis, False
308 # Name the tests this diff actually broke. The raw summary tail lists
309 # every FAILED line, pre-existing ones included, and a rewrite spec
310 # built from it sends the next coder to fix tests it did not break —
311 # often outside its own declared files. The baseline is what tells
312 # them apart, so spend it here too, not only on the routing decision.
313 diagnosis = f"preflight failed (regression): {exc.reason}"
314 if comparison.new_failures:
315 named = "\n".join(f" {test_id}" for test_id in sorted(comparison.new_failures))
316 diagnosis += f"\nnew failures introduced by this diff:\n{named}"
317 if summary_tail:
318 diagnosis += f"\n{summary_tail}"
319 if comparison.new_failures:
320 diagnosis += (
321 "\nAny FAILED line above that is not in the list of new failures was "
322 "already red on the launch branch — it is not yours to fix."
323 )
324 return diagnosis, True
325
326 async def _resolve_conflict_in_place(self, exc: MergeConflict) -> bool:
327 """One warm-resume attempt at the group's own coder session (plan U1),
328 tried before falling back to a full spec rewrite: the session that just
329 built this work still holds full context of it. Returns True when the
330 coder finished cleanly and the merge should be retried; False when the
331 resume/report itself failed, so the caller falls straight through to
332 escalate-then-rewrite without a second merge attempt."""
333 assert self.workspace is not None
334 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: attempting in-place conflict resolution")
335 try:
336 result = await asyncio.to_thread(
337 self.deps.runner.resume,
338 session_id=self.coder_sid,
339 prompt=render_conflict_resolve_prompt(
340 self.group,
341 conflict_summary=str(exc),
342 integration_branch=integration_branch(self.deps.run_id),
343 ),
344 cwd=self.workspace,
345 on_turn=self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry),
346 )
347 report, _ = await asyncio.to_thread(
348 nudge_until_report,
349 self.deps.runner,
350 result,
351 CoderReport,
352 cwd=self.workspace,
353 verification_ids=[item.id for item in self.group.verification],
354 )
355 except SessionError as inner_exc:
356 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: conflict resolve attempt failed: {inner_exc}")
357 return False
358 self._persist_coder_usage()
359 self._spread(report.surprises)
360 if report.status != "completed":
361 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: conflict resolve ended ({report.status})")
362 return False
363 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: conflict resolve attempt reported completed")
364 return True
365

367def _short_test_summary(output: str) -> str:
368 """The "short test summary info" tail of a pytest run's captured output
369 (plan U3/F18) — the FAILED/ERROR lines and the final result line, not the
370 full scrollback. Empty when the marker never appears, e.g. an env/timeout
371 failure that produced no pytest output at all."""
372 marker = "short test summary info"
373 idx = output.find(marker)
374 if idx == -1:
375 return ""
376 line_end = output.find("\n", idx)
377 if line_end == -1:
378 return ""
379 return output[line_end + 1 :].strip()
380

382def _move_paths(worktree: Path, paths: list[str], dest_dir: Path) -> None:
383 """Move ``paths`` (relative, as ``git status --porcelain`` names them — a
384 directory carries a trailing slash) out of ``worktree`` into ``dest_dir``,
385 keeping their relative layout."""
386 for rel in paths:
387 source = worktree / rel.rstrip("/")
388 if not source.exists():
389 continue
390 target = dest_dir / rel.rstrip("/")
391 target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
392 if target.exists():
393 if target.is_dir():
394 shutil.rmtree(target)
395 else:
396 target.unlink()
397 shutil.move(str(source), str(target))
398
399
400def _is_retry(response: EscalationResponse | None) -> bool:
401 return response is not None and response.action == HumanAction.RETRY
402

404def _operator_surprise(group_id: str, answer: str) -> Surprise:
405 """Fold an operator's free-text guidance into the next rewrite as a surprise —
406 no ``rewrite_spec`` signature change (plan Phase D)."""
407 return Surprise(kind="other", description=f"[operator] {answer}", affected_groups=[group_id])

1211 def _classify_preflight(self, exc: PreflightFailure) -> tuple[str, bool]:
1212 """Route a preflight failure by cause (plan U3): ``env``/``timeout``
1213 never ran a real test, and a ``regression`` whose failing tests are all
1214 already red on the launch branch is not evidence about this diff
1215 either — neither is attributable, and the caller must not spend a
1216 rewrite on it. Only a genuinely new, run failure is attributable.
1217
1218 Returns the diagnosis text handed to the next generation (or the
1219 operator) — carrying the check output's own "short test summary info"
1220 tail, not just a path to the log — and whether the failure is
1221 attributable.
1222 """
1223 summary_tail = ""
1224 if exc.output_path is not None and exc.output_path.is_file():
1225 summary_tail = _short_test_summary(exc.output_path.read_text())
1226 if exc.kind in ("env", "timeout", "untracked"):
1227 diagnosis = f"preflight failed ({exc.kind}): {exc.reason}"
1228 if summary_tail:
1229 diagnosis += f"\n{summary_tail}"
1230 return diagnosis, False
1231 # kind == "regression": tests actually ran and something actually
1232 # failed — the only question left is whether it is new. The gate
1233 # already answered that (it had to, to decide whether to raise), so
1234 # take its verdict rather than re-deriving one: re-derivation guessed a
1235 # single `preflight-junit.xml` beside the log and so was blind to the
1236 # UI steps' own reports. The fallback covers a `PreflightFailure`
1237 # raised from somewhere other than `run_preflight`.
1238 comparison = exc.comparison
1239 if comparison is None:
1240 junit_path = (
1241 exc.output_path.parent / "preflight-junit.xml"
1242 if exc.output_path is not None
1243 else None
1244 )
1245 failing = (
1246 failing_tests_from_junit(junit_path) if junit_path is not None else frozenset()
1247 )
1248 comparison = compare_to_baseline(self.deps.preflight_baseline, failing)
1249 if comparison.verdict == "pre_existing":
1250 diagnosis = (
1251 f"preflight failed (pre-existing): {exc.reason} — every failing test was "
1252 "already failing on the launch branch"
1253 )
1254 if summary_tail:
1255 diagnosis += f"\n{summary_tail}"
1256 return diagnosis, False
1257 # Name the tests this diff actually broke. The raw summary tail lists
1258 # every FAILED line, pre-existing ones included, and a rewrite spec
1259 # built from it sends the next coder to fix tests it did not break —
1260 # often outside its own declared files. The baseline is what tells
1261 # them apart, so spend it here too, not only on the routing decision.
1262 diagnosis = f"preflight failed (regression): {exc.reason}"
1263 if comparison.new_failures:
1264 named = "\n".join(f" {test_id}" for test_id in sorted(comparison.new_failures))
1265 diagnosis += f"\nnew failures introduced by this diff:\n{named}"
1266 if summary_tail:
1267 diagnosis += f"\n{summary_tail}"
1268 if comparison.new_failures:
1269 diagnosis += (
1270 "\nAny FAILED line above that is not in the list of new failures was "
1271 "already red on the launch branch — it is not yours to fix."
1272 )
1273 return diagnosis, True

  • Summary: orchestrator/execution/escalating.py owns the EscalationHandlers mixin (_escalate, _approve_gate, _diff, _resolve_needs_input, _on_content_filtered, _on_coder_stuck, _on_reviewer_hard, _rewrite, _relaunch, _persist_rewritten_spec, _decisions_text, _advance_generation) and the helpers _context_surprise, _is_retry, _operator_surprise, which the merge ladder now imports from it; the existing execution/escalation.py (broker and policy transport) keeps its name and is not touched.

6helpers are shared with `merge_ladder.py`, the one inter-mixin import edge.
