42class EscalationHandlers:
43 """Escalation broker calls, approval gates, rewrite and relaunch."""
44
45 deps: ReviewDeps
46 ctx: GroupContext
47 group: Group
48 gid: str
49 generation: int
50 workspace: Path | None
51 coder_sid: str
52 coder_entry: SessionEntry | None
53 handoff_prompt: str | None
54 rewrites: int
55 sessions_spawned: int
56 _questions: int
57 _operator_notes: list[str]
58 _current_round_no: int
59 _heartbeat: RoundHeartbeat
60 _log: Callable[[str], None]
61 _round_tag: Callable[[int], str]
62 _spread: Callable[[list[Surprise]], None]
63 _worker_call: Callable[..., Awaitable[RoundResult]]
64 _make_coder_on_turn: Callable[[SessionEntry | None], object]
65
66 async def _escalate(
67 self,
68 kind: EscalationKind,
69 *,
70 prompt: str,
71 report_path: str | None = None,
72 verdict_path: str | None = None,
73 surprises: list[Surprise] | None = None,
74 want_diff: bool = False,
75 ) -> EscalationResponse | None:
76 """Escalate ``kind`` to the operator if the policy dictates.
77
78 Returns the operator's ``answer`` or ``retry`` response (callers that can
79 relaunch the same spec check ``_is_retry``; every other site treats the two
80 alike), or ``None`` when the caller must run its autonomous path —
81 escalation is off for this kind, or a timeout with ``on_timeout =
82 autonomous`` fired. ``skip`` (→ GroupFailure) and ``abort`` (→ RunAbort)
83 are raised here and never returned. When broker/policy are
84 absent the check short-circuits with zero side effects, so an autonomous run
85 is byte-identical to pre-Phase-D."""
86 policy, broker = self.deps.policy, self.deps.broker
87 if broker is None or policy is None or not policy.should_escalate(kind):
88 return None
89 context = EscalationContext(
90 report_path=report_path,
91 verdict_path=verdict_path,
92 diff_summary=self._diff() if want_diff else "",
93 surprises=list(surprises or []),
94 )
95 request = EscalationRequest(
96 id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:12],
97 run_id=self.deps.run_id,
98 group_id=self.gid,
99 generation=self.generation,
100 kind=kind,
101 prompt=prompt,
102 context=context,
103 )
104 response = await asyncio.to_thread(broker.raise_escalation, request)
105 if response is None:
106 return None # timeout → autonomous fallback
107 if response.action == HumanAction.ABORT:
108 broker.trigger_abort() # release every sibling waiter before we unwind
109 raise RunAbort(f"operator aborted the run at group {self.gid} ({kind.value})")
110 if response.action == HumanAction.SKIP:
111 raise GroupFailure(f"operator skipped group {self.gid} ({kind.value})")
112 return response
113
114 async def _approve_gate(self, kind: EscalationKind, prompt: str) -> None:
115 """Interactive-tier approval gate: an ``answer`` or ``retry`` (or a
116 non-escalating tier) means proceed; ``skip``/``abort`` raise inside
117 ``_escalate``."""
118 await self._escalate(kind, prompt=prompt)
119
120 def _diff(self) -> str:
121 if self.workspace is None:
122 return ""
123 return diff_stat(self.workspace, self.deps.base_ref_for(self.group))
124
125 async def _resolve_needs_input(self, report: CoderReport) -> RoundResult | None:
126 """Coder ended its turn with a question. Returns the resumed RoundResult so
127 the warm loop continues, or None when the generation is abandoned (an
128 operator answer folded into a rewrite, or the question treated as a block
129 when no human answered)."""
130 assert self.workspace is not None
131 self._questions += 1
132 report_path = self.deps.store.save_group_artifact(
133 self.gid, f"report-g{self.generation}-q{self._questions}.json", report
134 )
135 self._spread(report.surprises)
136 question = report.question or report.summary or "(no question text)"
137 # orchestrator_only owns the human channel: downgrade the question to the
138 # blocked/rewrite path instead of a warm coder resume.
139 downgraded = self.deps.policy is not None and self.deps.policy.source == "orchestrator_only"
140 kind = EscalationKind.CODER_BLOCKED if downgraded else EscalationKind.CODER_QUESTION
141 response = await self._escalate(
142 kind,
143 prompt=f'coder for {self.gid} needs input: "{question}"',
144 report_path=str(report_path),
145 )
146 if response is not None and not downgraded:
147 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.RUNNING)
148 answer_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry)
149 return await self._worker_call(
150 partial(
151 self.deps.runner.resume,
152 session_id=self.coder_sid,
153 prompt=render_coder_answer_prompt(response.answer),
154 cwd=self.workspace,
155 on_turn=answer_on_turn,
156 ),
157 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
158 session_id=sid,
159 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
160 cwd=self.workspace,
161 on_turn=answer_on_turn,
162 ),
163 )
164 if _is_retry(response):
165 await self._relaunch(response.answer, f"coder needs input: {question}")
166 return None
167 extra = [_context_surprise(self.gid, f"coder needs_input: {question}")]
168 if response is not None:
169 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
170 await self._rewrite(f"coder needs input: {question}", extra=extra)
171 return None
172
173 async def _on_content_filtered(self, exc: ContentFiltered) -> None:
174 """The API's content filter blocked a coder or reviewer round (plan
175 U10) — routed like a blocked coder, quoting the last thing the model
176 actually said, and never warm-resumed: the session that produced the
177 blocked output is not one to retry as-is."""
178 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(self._current_round_no)}: ended (content filter)")
179 text = exc.last_assistant_text[:1000]
180 response = await self._escalate(
181 EscalationKind.CODER_BLOCKED,
182 prompt=f'coder for {self.gid} hit the API content filter — last assistant message: "{text}"',
183 want_diff=True,
184 )
185 if _is_retry(response):
186 await self._relaunch(response.answer, "API content filter")
187 return
188 extra = [
189 _context_surprise(
190 self.gid,
191 f"API content filter blocked the coder's output; last message: {text}",
192 )
193 ]
194 if response is not None:
195 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
196 await self._rewrite("content filter", extra=extra)
197
198 async def _on_coder_stuck(self, report: CoderReport, report_path: Path) -> None:
199 """A blocked/failed coder report: escalate, then rewrite (guided if answered)
200 — or relaunch the same spec when the operator says ``retry``."""
201 response = await self._escalate(
202 EscalationKind.CODER_BLOCKED,
203 prompt=f"coder for {self.gid} reported {report.status}: {report.summary}",
204 report_path=str(report_path),
205 want_diff=True,
206 )
207 if _is_retry(response):
208 await self._relaunch(response.answer, f"coder reported status {report.status}")
209 return
210 extra = [_context_surprise(self.gid, f"coder {report.status}: {report.summary}")]
211 if response is not None:
212 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
213 await self._rewrite(f"coder reported status {report.status}", extra=extra)
214
215 async def _on_reviewer_hard(self, verdict: ReviewerVerdict, verdict_path: Path | None) -> None:
216 """A too_hard/structural verdict: escalate, then rewrite (guided if answered)
217 — or relaunch the same spec when the operator says ``retry``."""
218 kind = (
219 EscalationKind.REVIEWER_TOO_HARD
220 if verdict.status == "too_hard"
221 else EscalationKind.REVIEWER_STRUCTURAL
222 )
223 response = await self._escalate(
224 kind,
225 prompt=f"reviewer for {self.gid} returned {verdict.status}: {verdict.notes}",
226 verdict_path=str(verdict_path) if verdict_path is not None else None,
227 want_diff=True,
228 )
229 if _is_retry(response):
230 await self._relaunch(response.answer, f"reviewer verdict: {verdict.status}")
231 return
232 extra = [_context_surprise(self.gid, f"reviewer {verdict.status}: {verdict.notes}")]
233 if response is not None:
234 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
235 await self._rewrite(f"reviewer verdict: {verdict.status}", extra=extra)
236
237 async def _rewrite(self, why: str, extra: list[Surprise] | None = None) -> None:
238 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.REWRITING)
239 extra = list(extra or [])
240 if self.rewrites >= self.deps.execution.max_rewrites:
241 # Terminal give-up: escalate before failing. An answer grants one more
242 # (guided) rewrite; None (unescalated / autonomous timeout) fails as before.
243 response = await self._escalate(
244 EscalationKind.CAPS_EXHAUSTED,
245 prompt=(
246 f"group {self.gid}: rewrite cap ({self.deps.execution.max_rewrites}) "
247 f"exhausted — {why}"
248 ),
249 want_diff=True,
250 )
251 if response is None:
252 raise GroupFailure(
253 f"rewrite cap ({self.deps.execution.max_rewrites}) exhausted: {why}"
254 )
255 # `answer` and `retry` alike grant the one extra rewrite.
256 extra.append(_operator_surprise(self.gid, response.answer))
257 surprises = self.deps.board.consume(self.gid) + extra
258 self._log(
259 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: rewriting spec ({why}); "
260 f"surprises consumed: {len(surprises)} "
261 f"[{', '.join(surprise.kind for surprise in surprises) or 'none'}]"
262 )
263 self.group = await asyncio.to_thread(self.deps.rewrite_spec, self.group, surprises)
264 self.rewrites += 1
265 self.handoff_prompt = None # the fresh session gets the rewritten spec
266 if self.sessions_spawned:
267 self._advance_generation()
268 self._persist_rewritten_spec()
269
270 async def _relaunch(self, note: str, why: str) -> None:
271 """Operator ``retry``: the cause was fixed outside the worker, so relaunch a
272 fresh coder on the *same* spec — no rewrite spent, no speccer call. The
273 note rides along as an ``## Operator note`` in the next prompt."""
274 self._log(
275 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: relaunching on the same spec "
276 f"(operator retry: {why})"
277 )
278 if note:
279 self._operator_notes.append(note)
280 self.handoff_prompt = None # the fresh session gets the unchanged spec
281 if self.sessions_spawned:
282 self._advance_generation()
283
284 def _persist_rewritten_spec(self) -> None:
285 """Save the rewritten spec beside the group so a post-mortem can
286 reconstruct what the coder was actually told (plan U14) — the group's
287 entry in ``groups.json`` stays the immutable grouper output and is
288 never rewritten. These ``spec-gen<N>.json`` files are the durable
289 record every restart path reads back through ``effective_group``
290 (resume, ``finish``, ``retry``), so this must run before the rewritten
291 group's next worktree is created — ``_rewrite`` calls it synchronously,
292 before any new generation launches."""
293 path = self.deps.store.paths.group_dir(self.gid) / f"spec-gen{self.generation}.json"
294 atomic_write_text(path, self.group.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n")
295
296 def _decisions_text(self) -> str:
297 """Binding operator decisions for this group, rendered fresh from disk
298 at every prompt build (plan U9) so a later answer reaches every
299 subsequent coder, handoff, reviewer and re-review prompt."""
300 return render_decisions_section(decision_ledger(self.deps.store.paths, self.gid))
301
302 def _advance_generation(self) -> None:
303 self.generation += 1
304 self.ctx.set_generation(self.generation)
305
306
307def _context_surprise(group_id: str, description: str) -> Surprise:
308 """Escalation context handed to the speccer when the group itself triggered
309 the rewrite (blocked/too_hard/structural) and no upstream surprise exists."""
310 return Surprise(kind="other", description=description, affected_groups=[group_id])
311
312
313def _is_retry(response: EscalationResponse | None) -> bool:
314 return response is not None and response.action == HumanAction.RETRY
315
316
317def _operator_surprise(group_id: str, answer: str) -> Surprise:
318 """Fold an operator's free-text guidance into the next rewrite as a surprise —
319 no ``rewrite_spec`` signature change (plan Phase D)."""
320 return Surprise(kind="other", description=f"[operator] {answer}", affected_groups=[group_id])

1246 """Escalate ``kind`` to the operator if the policy dictates.
1247
1248 Returns the operator's ``answer`` or ``retry`` response (callers that can
1249 relaunch the same spec check ``_is_retry``; every other site treats the two
1250 alike), or ``None`` when the caller must run its autonomous path —
1251 escalation is off for this kind, or a timeout with ``on_timeout =
1252 autonomous`` fired. ``skip`` (→ GroupFailure) and ``abort`` (→ RunAbort)
1253 are raised here and never returned. When broker/policy are
1254 absent the check short-circuits with zero side effects, so an autonomous run
1255 is byte-identical to pre-Phase-D."""
1256 policy, broker = self.deps.policy, self.deps.broker
1257 if broker is None or policy is None or not policy.should_escalate(kind):
1258 return None
1259 context = EscalationContext(
1260 report_path=report_path,
1261 verdict_path=verdict_path,
1262 diff_summary=self._diff() if want_diff else "",
1263 surprises=list(surprises or []),

1265 request = EscalationRequest(
1266 id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:12],
1267 run_id=self.deps.run_id,
1268 group_id=self.gid,
1269 generation=self.generation,
1270 kind=kind,
1271 prompt=prompt,
1272 context=context,
1273 )

1276 return None # timeout → autonomous fallback
1277 if response.action == HumanAction.ABORT:
1278 broker.trigger_abort() # release every sibling waiter before we unwind
1279 raise RunAbort(f"operator aborted the run at group {self.gid} ({kind.value})")
1280 if response.action == HumanAction.SKIP:

113def test_execution_modules_import_graph_is_acyclic():
114 """Static import graph over the split modules; `merge_ladder -> escalating`
115 is the one allowed inter-mixin edge. `TYPE_CHECKING` imports are skipped."""
116 import ast
117
118 names = ["surprises", "merge_ladder", "escalating", "host", "review"]
119 root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "orchestrator" / "execution"
120 graph: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
121 for name in names:
122 tree = ast.parse((root / f"{name}.py").read_text())
123 deps: set[str] = set()
124 for node in tree.body:
125 if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
126 mod = node.module.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
127 if node.module.startswith("orchestrator.execution") and mod in names:
128 deps.add(mod)
129 graph[name] = deps
130 assert graph["merge_ladder"] & {"surprises", "escalating"} == {"escalating"}
131 assert graph["escalating"] == set()
132 assert graph["surprises"] == set()
133
134 visiting: set[str] = set()
135 done: set[str] = set()
136
137 def visit(node: str) -> None:
138 assert node not in visiting, f"import cycle through {node}"
139 if node in done:
140 return
141 visiting.add(node)
142 for dep in graph[node]:
143 visit(dep)
144 visiting.discard(node)
145 done.add(node)
146
147 for name in names:
148 visit(name)

u4: `orchestrator/execution/records.py` owns the `SessionRecords` mixin (`_record`, `_copy_usage`, `_persist_coder_usage`, `_persist_reviewer_usage`, `_make_coder_on_turn`, `_adopt_actual_session_id`, `_refresh_transcript`, `_watch_transcript`, `_round_tag`, `_log_coder_session_end`) plus `_transcript_str` and `_spec_hash`; `orchestrator/execution/reviewer.py` owns the `ReviewerRound` mixin (`_review_round`, `_archive_review_scratch`); `review.py` re-exports `_spec_hash` transitionally.

Plan section U4

U4. records-and-reviewer — session records, usage and transcript bookkeeping move to execution/records.py; the reviewer round moves to execution/reviewer.py

  • Summary: orchestrator/execution/records.py owns the SessionRecords mixin (_record, _copy_usage, _persist_coder_usage, _persist_reviewer_usage, _make_coder_on_turn, _adopt_actual_session_id, _refresh_transcript, _watch_transcript, _round_tag, _log_coder_session_end) plus _transcript_str and _spec_hash; orchestrator/execution/reviewer.py owns the ReviewerRound mixin (_review_round, _archive_review_scratch); review.py re-exports _spec_hash transitionally.

orchestrator/execution/records.py
@@ -0,0 +1,240 @@
1"""Session records: manifest entries, per-session usage and transcript bookkeeping (plan U4).
2
3`SessionRecords` is a mixin with no `__init__`: every attribute it reads is
4declared below and born in the composition root (`ExecutionHost`).
5"""
6
7from __future__ import annotations
8
9import hashlib
10from collections.abc import Callable
11from datetime import UTC, datetime
12from pathlib import Path
13from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
14
15from orchestrator.execution.heartbeat import RoundHeartbeat
16from orchestrator.execution.manifest import record_session
17from orchestrator.execution.prompting import (
18 render_ladder_compact_prompt,
19 render_ladder_prioritized_prompt,
20 render_ladder_summary_prompt,
21)
22from orchestrator.execution.sessions import RoundResult, SessionRunner, session_display_name
23from orchestrator.execution.streaming import TurnUsage
24from orchestrator.model import Group, SessionEntry, SessionRole
25
26
27if TYPE_CHECKING:
28 from orchestrator.execution.review import ReviewDeps
29
30
31class SessionRecords:
32 deps: ReviewDeps
33 gid: str
34 generation: int
35 workspace: Path | None
36 coder_sid: str
37 coder_entry: SessionEntry | None
38 sessions_spawned: int
39 _current_round_no: int
40 _heartbeat: RoundHeartbeat
41 _log: Callable[[str], None]
42
43 def _copy_usage(self, entry: SessionEntry, session_id: str) -> None:
44 """Mirror the in-memory cumulative usage onto a manifest entry.
45
46 ``last_context_tokens`` is the breaker's input (occupancy of the latest
47 round); the cumulative counters are the session's total spend, kept split
48 by token class so an estimate-vs-actual view can tell a cache-heavy run
49 from an genuinely expensive one. Both are written on the same save.
50 """
51 usage = self.deps.runner.usage_of(session_id)
52 entry.last_context_tokens = usage.last_context_tokens
53 entry.rounds_completed = usage.rounds
54 entry.total_input_tokens = usage.total_input_tokens
55 entry.total_output_tokens = usage.total_output_tokens
56 entry.total_cache_read_tokens = usage.total_cache_read_tokens
57 entry.total_cache_creation_tokens = usage.total_cache_creation_tokens
58 entry.base_context_tokens = usage.base_context_tokens
59 entry.total_cost_usd = usage.total_cost_usd
60
61 def _persist_coder_usage(self) -> None:
62 """Record the active coder's latest context size on its manifest entry
63 after every round (R5): in-memory usage dies with the process, and the
64 next re-entry pre-checks this value against the breaker limit."""
65 if self.coder_entry is None:
66 return
67 self._copy_usage(self.coder_entry, self.coder_sid)
68 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
69
70 def _make_coder_on_turn(
71 self, entry: SessionEntry
72 ) -> Callable[[TurnUsage, Callable[[str], None]], None]:
73 """Per-turn observer for one coder round call (plan U1's seam), doing two
74 unrelated things that happen to ride the same callback:
75
76 - continuous bookkeeping (plan U4): ``last_context_tokens`` updates as
77 turns stream in, not only once the round finishes and
78 ``_persist_coder_usage`` runs — so a group's manifest entry reflects
79 reality while it is still in flight, not just after.
80 - the staged context ladder (plan U3), gated by
81 ``breaker.context_ladder_enabled`` (off by default): 70%/90%/100% of
82 ``context_token_limit`` each send at most one staged prompt onto the
83 still-running round via ``send``. This bounds *cost* inside a round —
84 a token ceiling is a proxy for cost, not for stuck, which is why R7
85 rejected a wall-clock timeout here for the opposite reason.
86
87 ``fired`` is local to this call, so a fresh round always gets its own
88 clean set of thresholds — a round sitting at 99% from a prior round
89 never suppresses this round's own 70% checkpoint.
90 """
91 fired: set[str] = set()
92
93 def on_turn(usage: TurnUsage, send: Callable[[str], None]) -> None:
94 context = (
95 usage.input_tokens
96 + usage.output_tokens
97 + usage.cache_read_input_tokens
98 + usage.cache_creation_input_tokens
99 )
100 entry.last_context_tokens = context
101 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
102 if not self.deps.breaker.context_ladder_enabled:
103 return
104 limit = self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit
105 if context >= limit and "100" not in fired:
106 fired.update({"70", "90", "100"})
107 send(render_ladder_compact_prompt())
108 elif context >= limit * 0.9 and "90" not in fired:
109 fired.update({"70", "90"})
110 send(render_ladder_prioritized_prompt())
111 elif context >= limit * 0.7 and "70" not in fired:
112 fired.add("70")
113 send(render_ladder_summary_prompt())
114
115 return on_turn
116
117 def _adopt_actual_session_id(self, result: RoundResult) -> None:
118 """Reconcile the pre-registered coder id with the one the CLI really used.
119
120 Plan U7 records the id *before* the fork, which assumes the fork uses it.
121 A usage-limit retry breaks that assumption: the first attempt spends the
122 id, so the retry mints a fresh one (see ``_call_with_retry``). Without
123 this, the manifest keeps an id no session was ever created under, and a
124 later resume would `--resume` into nothing — turning a recovered run
125 into an unrecoverable one.
126 """
127 actual = result.session_id
128 if not actual or actual == self.coder_sid:
129 return
130 self._log(
131 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: coder session is {actual}, "
132 f"not the pre-registered {self.coder_sid} (usage-limit retry minted a new id)"
133 )
134 self.coder_sid = actual
135 self.coder_entry.session_id = actual
136
137 def _refresh_transcript(self, entry: SessionEntry) -> None:
138 """Fill in a pre-registered entry's transcript path once its session
139 actually exists on disk (plan U7) — recorded before the fork call, so
140 the path itself isn't known until the call returns.
141
142 Authoritative over whatever `_watch_transcript` filled early (F9): a
143 usage-limit retry can mint a fresh session id mid-fork, making the
144 heartbeat's early path provisional — this overwrite, keyed on the
145 adopted id, is what settles it."""
146 self._heartbeat.on_tick = None
147 entry.transcript_path = _transcript_str(self.deps.runner, entry.session_id)
148 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
149
150 def _watch_transcript(self, entry: SessionEntry) -> None:
151 """Fill ``transcript_path`` while the fork is still blocking (F9).
152
153 `start_fork` blocks for the round's entire first turn — 8 to 24 minutes
154 on r20260828-090936 — and until it returns the transcript endpoint 404s,
155 so the operator cannot watch the very work they are waiting on. The
156 transcript *file* appears as soon as the CLI starts writing; only the
157 manifest pointer is missing. The group's heartbeat thread is the one
158 thing awake during the fork, so it re-globs for the pre-registered id
159 each tick and persists the path the moment the file exists. The hook
160 self-clears once it has done its job; `_refresh_transcript` clears it
161 unconditionally and overwrites the path after the fork returns."""
162
163 def probe() -> None:
164 if entry.transcript_path:
165 self._heartbeat.on_tick = None
166 return
167 path = _transcript_str(self.deps.runner, entry.session_id)
168 if path is not None:
169 entry.transcript_path = path
170 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
171 self._heartbeat.on_tick = None
172
173 self._heartbeat.on_tick = probe
174
175 def _persist_reviewer_usage(self, session_id: str) -> None:
176 """Record the reviewer's latest context size on its manifest entry after
177 every round (plan U7), mirroring ``_persist_coder_usage``: the reviewer
178 entry otherwise carries a zero context-token count forever."""
179 group_entry = self.deps.manifest.groups.get(self.gid)
180 if group_entry is None:
181 return
182 for entry in reversed(group_entry.sessions):
183 if entry.role == SessionRole.REVIEWER and entry.session_id == session_id:
184 self._copy_usage(entry, session_id)
185 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
186 return
187
188 def _log_coder_session_end(self) -> None:
189 """One line per coder session with what it cost — the run log used to
190 carry no cost at all, and four of six run notes said so."""
191 if self.coder_entry is None:
192 return
193 entry = self.coder_entry
194 rounds = "round" if entry.rounds_completed == 1 else "rounds"
195 self._log(
196 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: coder session ended — "
197 f"{entry.rounds_completed} {rounds}, ${entry.total_cost_usd:.2f}"
198 )
199
200 def _round_tag(self, round_no: int) -> str:
201 # Side effect: records the round currently in flight (plan U10), so
202 # `_on_content_filtered` can log the round a `ContentFiltered` ended
203 # without a second, separate tracker to keep in sync with this one.
204 self._current_round_no = round_no
205 return f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation} round {round_no}"
206
207 def _record(self, role: SessionRole, session_id: str) -> SessionEntry:
208 # started_at/model land here, at creation (plan U4) — not only once the
209 # first round completes — so an in-flight group is distinguishable from
210 # one that never started, and a crash before any round finishes still
211 # leaves a manifest entry an operator can date.
212 entry = SessionEntry(
213 session_id=session_id,
214 role=role,
215 generation=self.generation,
216 name=session_display_name(self.deps.run_id, self.gid, role.value, self.generation),
217 transcript_path=_transcript_str(self.deps.runner, session_id),
218 started_at=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
219 model=self.deps.runner.model,
220 )
221 record_session(
222 self.deps.manifest,
223 group_id=self.gid,
224 group_name=self.group.name,
225 summary=self.group.summary,
226 entry=entry,
227 )
228 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
229 self.sessions_spawned += 1
230 return entry
231
232
233def _transcript_str(runner: SessionRunner, session_id: str) -> str | None:
234 path = runner.transcript_path(session_id)
235 return str(path) if path is not None else None
236
237
238def _spec_hash(group: Group) -> str:
239 """Identity of the spec a coder was launched on (see ``SessionEntry.spec_sha256``)."""
240 return hashlib.sha256(group.model_dump_json().encode()).hexdigest()

872 async def _review_round(
873 self, report_path: Path, rounds: int
874 ) -> tuple[ReviewerVerdict | None, Path | None]:
875 if self.group.intensity == ReviewIntensity.SELF_VERIFY:
876 return None, None # AE7: no reviewer session is ever created
877 assert self.workspace is not None
878 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.REVIEWING)
879 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("reviewer verifying the report") # F4
880
881 def _reviewer_recover(sid: str) -> RoundResult:
882 return self.deps.runner.resume(
883 session_id=sid,
884 prompt=render_re_review_prompt(str(report_path), decisions=self._decisions_text()),
885 cwd=self.workspace,
886 )
887
888 if self.reviewer_sid is None:
889 first = await self._worker_call(
890 partial(
891 self._launch_call(),
892 prompt=render_reviewer_prompt(
893 self.deps.run_id,
894 self.group,
895 report_path=str(report_path),
896 base_ref=self.deps.base_ref_for(self.group),
897 scratch_dir=str(self.workspace / REVIEW_SCRATCH_DIRNAME),
898 decisions=self._decisions_text(),
899 ),
900 name=session_display_name(
901 self.deps.run_id, self.gid, "reviewer", self.generation
902 ),
903 cwd=self.workspace,
904 ),
905 recover=_reviewer_recover,
906 )
907 self.reviewer_sid = first.session_id
908 self._record(SessionRole.REVIEWER, first.session_id)
909 result = first
910 else:
911 result = await self._worker_call(
912 partial(
913 self.deps.runner.resume,
914 session_id=self.reviewer_sid,
915 prompt=render_re_review_prompt(
916 str(report_path), decisions=self._decisions_text()
917 ),
918 cwd=self.workspace,
919 ),
920 recover=_reviewer_recover,
921 )
922
923 def _reviewer_nudge(round_result: RoundResult) -> tuple[ReviewerVerdict, RoundResult]:
924 return nudge_until_report(
925 self.deps.runner, round_result, ReviewerVerdict, cwd=self.workspace
926 )
927
928 def _reviewer_nudge_recover(sid: str) -> tuple[ReviewerVerdict, RoundResult]:
929 return _reviewer_nudge(_reviewer_recover(sid))
930
931 verdict, result = await self._worker_call(
932 partial(_reviewer_nudge, result), recover=_reviewer_nudge_recover
933 )
934 self._persist_reviewer_usage(self.reviewer_sid)
935 verdict_path = self.deps.store.save_group_artifact(
936 self.gid, artifact_name("verdict", self.generation, rounds), verdict
937 )
938 self._spread(verdict.surprises)
939 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: reviewer verdict {verdict.status}")
940
941 if (
942 verdict.status == "approved"
943 and self.group.intensity == ReviewIntensity.PAIRED_PLUS
944 and not self.extra_pass_done
945 ):
946 # Above d_hard: one mandatory extra verification round (origin R15).
947 self.extra_pass_done = True
948 result = await self._worker_call(
949 partial(
950 self.deps.runner.resume,
951 session_id=self.reviewer_sid,
952 prompt=render_extra_pass_prompt(),
953 cwd=self.workspace,
954 ),
955 recover=_reviewer_recover,
956 )
957 verdict, result = await self._worker_call(
958 partial(_reviewer_nudge, result), recover=_reviewer_nudge_recover
959 )

1"""The generation lifecycle: one coder session's whole run from launch (or
2warm re-entry) through rounds, the breaker, and the terminal handoff into the
3next generation (plan U5 of the review-loop split).
4
5`GenerationLoop` is mixed onto `_GroupExecution`, whose `__init__` is the
6only place the attributes below are born (see `ExecutionHost`).
7"""

57class _ContentFilterStop(Exception):
58 """Loop-internal signal (plan U10): `_worker_call` converts a
59 `ContentFiltered` into this before it can reach a caller's own
60 `except SessionError` — deliberately *not* a `SessionError` subclass, so
61 `_reenter`'s fallback (which catches `SessionError`) never mistakes a
62 content-filtered session for merely unreachable. `_run_generation`
63 catches it once, at the top of every generation."""
64
65 def __init__(self, exc: ContentFiltered):
66 super().__init__(str(exc))
67 self.exc = exc
68

70class GenerationLoop:
71 """One group's generations: launch/re-entry, the coder-reviewer round
72 loop, the breaker, and the handoff into the next generation."""
73
74 deps: ReviewDeps
75 ctx: GroupContext
76 group: Group
77 gid: str
78 generation: int
79 sessions_spawned: int
80 handoff_prompt: str | None
81 workspace: Path | None
82 coder_sid: str
83 coder_entry: SessionEntry | None
84 reviewer_sid: str | None
85 _env_failure: str | None
86 _grant_notes: list[str]
87 _flake_reruns: int
88 _reentry_entry: SessionEntry | None
89 _heartbeat: RoundHeartbeat
90 _log: Callable[[str], None]
91 _round_tag: Callable[[int], str]
92 _record: Callable[..., SessionEntry]
93 _spread: Callable[..., None]
94 _persist_coder_usage: Callable[[], None]
95 _make_coder_on_turn: Callable[[SessionEntry | None], object]
96 _adopt_actual_session_id: Callable[[RoundResult], None]
97 _refresh_transcript: Callable[[SessionEntry], None]
98 _watch_transcript: Callable[[SessionEntry], None]
99 _log_coder_session_end: Callable[[], None]
100 _decisions_text: Callable[[], str]
101 _resolve_needs_input: Callable[[CoderReport], Awaitable[RoundResult | None]]
102 _on_content_filtered: Callable[[ContentFiltered], Awaitable[None]]
103 _on_coder_stuck: Callable[[CoderReport, Path], Awaitable[None]]
104 _on_reviewer_hard: Callable[[ReviewerVerdict, Path | None], Awaitable[None]]
105 _review_round: Callable[..., Awaitable[tuple[ReviewerVerdict | None, Path | None]]]
106 _handle_pending_surprises: Callable[[str], Awaitable[bool]]
107 _apply_briefing: Callable[[str], str]
108 _apply_env_notice: Callable[[str], str]
109 _apply_operator_note: Callable[[str], str]
110 _approve_gate: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]
111 _escalate: Callable[..., Awaitable[object]]
112 _merge: Callable[[], Awaitable[bool]]
113 _advance_generation: Callable[[], None]
114
115 async def _worker_call(self, thunk: Callable[[], object], *, recover: Callable[[str], object]):
116 """Runs one worker call in a thread; on a Suspend Cure (plan U5) — the
117 liveness probe having killed this child because it showed no Sign of
118 Life since a detected machine wake — logs the recovery and re-issues
119 ``recover(cured_session_id)`` in *this call's* place, itself routed
120 back through ``_worker_call`` so a second cure re-issues again until
121 the probe's own per-generation cap stops curing. Coder call sites pass
122 a ``recover`` that warm-resumes with the re-entry prompt; reviewer
123 sites pass one that resumes with the re-review prompt (per the U5
124 decision) — the wrapper itself is role-agnostic.
125
126 A ``ContentFiltered`` (plan U10) is converted here to a loop-internal
127 ``_ContentFilterStop`` before it can reach a caller's own
128 ``except SessionError`` — most importantly ``_reenter``'s fallback,
129 which must never treat a content-filtered session as merely
130 unreachable and fork a fresh one from it. Any other exception — a
131 plain ``SessionError``, ``UsageLimit`` — propagates unchanged; this
132 wrapper is transparent to everything but ``SuspendCured`` and
133 ``ContentFiltered``. A ``SuspendCured`` from a first launch whose
134 session never registered on disk still carries a real ``session_id``
135 (read off the argv the failed call actually used, not off the
136 transcript), so ``recover`` resumes it the same as any other cure;
137 being a ``SessionError`` subclass, it would fall through to the
138 ordinary failure handling regardless if it ever turned up somewhere
139 this wrapper does not reach.
140 """
141 try:
142 return await asyncio.to_thread(thunk)
143 except ContentFiltered as exc:
144 raise _ContentFilterStop(exc) from exc
145 except SuspendCured as exc:
146 self._log(
147 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: "
148 f"warm-resuming session {exc.session_id} after suspend cure"
149 )
150 return await self._worker_call(partial(recover, exc.session_id), recover=recover)
151
152 async def run(self) -> GroupState:
153 # interactive tier only: approve before anything is launched.
154 await self._approve_gate(
155 EscalationKind.GROUP_START, f"launch group {self.gid} ({self.group.name})?"
156 )
157 await self._handle_pending_surprises("upstream surprise named this group before launch")
158 self.workspace = self.deps.workspace_for(self.group)
159 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: worktree ready at {self.workspace}")
160 if self.deps.provisioning_failure_for is not None:
161 self._env_failure = self.deps.provisioning_failure_for(self.group)
162 self._heartbeat.start()
163 # A usage-limit pause is announced on this group's heartbeat for as long
164 # as the group is live (see `UsageLimitGate.watch`) — a run that has
165 # stopped because the account is out of budget must read as *paused*,
166 # not as wedged, on the board as well as in the log.
167 gate = getattr(self.deps.runner, "gate", None)
168 if gate is not None:
169 gate.watch(self._heartbeat)
170 try:
171 while True:
172 merged = await self._run_generation()
173 if merged:
174 self._log_coder_session_end()
175 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: completed")
176 return GroupState.COMPLETED
177 # a rewrite or a retirement happened inside; loop spawns the next session
178 finally:
179 if gate is not None:
180 gate.unwatch(self._heartbeat)
181 self._heartbeat.stop()
182
183 # ------------------------------------------------------------ generation
184
185 async def _run_generation(self) -> bool:
186 """One coder session's lifetime. True → merged; False → respawn/rewritten.
187
188 A ``_ContentFilterStop`` (plan U10) can surface from any worker call
189 this generation makes — first launch, coder nudge, needs_input
190 resume, revision resume, or a reviewer call inside ``_review_round``
191 — so it is caught here, at the one place that wraps every one of
192 them, rather than at each call site individually.
193 """
194 try:
195 return await self._run_generation_body()
196 except _ContentFilterStop as exc:
197 await self._on_content_filtered(exc.exc)
198 return False
199
200 async def _run_generation_body(self) -> bool:
201 assert self.workspace is not None
202 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.RUNNING)
203 first: RoundResult | None = None
204 reentry, self._reentry_entry = self._reentry_entry, None # one-shot
205 is_reentry = reentry is not None
206 self._flake_reruns = 0
207 # Re-entry (warm-resumed or fallback-forked) continues this generation's
208 # numbering rather than starting over, so round-numbered artifacts don't
209 # collide with — and silently overwrite — pre-crash ones still on disk.
210 #
211 # Computed *before* the re-entry call, not after (plan P3): the re-entry
212 # resume is itself a full round — it writes files and runs tests, for
213 # twenty minutes on the run that prompted this — so it has to be able to
214 # announce its own number before it blocks. `completed_round_count` reads
215 # only the report artifacts already on disk and takes nothing from the
216 # resume, so hoisting it changes no number.
217 rounds = (
218 completed_round_count(self.deps.store.paths, self.gid, self.generation)
219 if is_reentry
220 else 0
221 )
222 if reentry is not None:
223 first = await self._reenter(reentry, round_no=rounds + 1)
224 if first is None:
225 prompt = self.handoff_prompt or render_coder_prompt(
226 self.deps.run_id, self.group, decisions=self._decisions_text()
227 )
228 prompt = self._apply_briefing(prompt)
229 prompt = self._apply_env_notice(prompt)
230 prompt = self._apply_operator_note(prompt)
231 self.handoff_prompt = None
232 # The session id is generated and recorded *before* the blocking fork
233 # call, not after (plan U7): a crash mid-call would otherwise leave no
234 # manifest entry for a group interrupted during its very first round,
235 # so a later resume would fork a brand new session instead of finding
236 # the one already under way.
237 self.coder_sid = str(uuid.uuid4())
238 self.reviewer_sid = None
239 self.coder_entry = self._record(SessionRole.CODER, self.coder_sid)
240 self.coder_entry.spec_sha256 = _spec_hash(self.group)
241 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
242 # Logged *before* the fork, not after. `start_fork` blocks for as long
243 # as the base session takes to absorb the group's prompt — 21 minutes
244 # on a real run — and the old "coder launched" line landed only once it
245 # returned, so a group killed mid-launch left a log that never
246 # mentioned it had started, and a live run showed a silent gap with no
247 # indication anything was happening.
248 launch = "forking base session" if self.deps.fork_base_session else "fresh session"
249 self._log(
250 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: "
251 f"coder launching, {launch} (session {self.coder_sid})"
252 )
253 # `round N: started` logged and marked *before* the fork call, not
254 # after — matching `_reenter`'s pattern. `start_fork` is itself round
255 # N's whole first turn, so logging it once the call returns leaves the
256 # round-start line trailing behind everything it is supposed to
257 # cover, and a group killed mid-fork looks like it never started a
258 # round at all.
259 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds + 1)}: started")
260 self._heartbeat.mark_round(self.generation, rounds + 1)
261 self._heartbeat.mark_phase(
262 "forking the base session" if self.deps.fork_base_session else "starting the coder"
263 )
264 self._watch_transcript(self.coder_entry)
265 coder_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry)
266 first = await self._worker_call(
267 partial(
268 self._launch_call(),
269 prompt=prompt,
270 name=session_display_name(self.deps.run_id, self.gid, "coder", self.generation),
271 cwd=self.workspace,
272 session_id=self.coder_sid,
273 on_turn=coder_on_turn,
274 ),
275 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
276 session_id=sid,
277 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
278 cwd=self.workspace,
279 on_turn=coder_on_turn,
280 ),
281 )
282 self._adopt_actual_session_id(first)
283 self._refresh_transcript(self.coder_entry)
284 self._log(f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: coder launched")
285 result = first
286 # Guarded on `is_reentry`, not on whether the resume succeeded: a
287 # fallback fork *is* round N of the same generation, and `_reenter`
288 # already announced N before it blocked. The fresh-fork branch above
289 # announces its own round before `start_fork` too, so nothing further is
290 # needed here in either case.
291
292 verification_ids = [item.id for item in self.group.verification]
293 while True:
294 # F4: nothing used to supersede "forking the base session" once the
295 # fork returned, so a finished round still read as mid-fork minutes
296 # later. Each pass through this loop is the coder producing (or
297 # being nudged toward) its report.
298 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("coder working toward a report")
299
300 def _coder_nudge(round_result: RoundResult) -> tuple[CoderReport, RoundResult]:
301 return nudge_until_report(
302 self.deps.runner,
303 round_result,
304 CoderReport,
305 cwd=self.workspace,
306 verification_ids=verification_ids,
307 )
308
309 def _coder_nudge_recover(sid: str) -> tuple[CoderReport, RoundResult]:
310 resumed = self.deps.runner.resume(
311 session_id=sid,
312 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
313 cwd=self.workspace,
314 on_turn=self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry),
315 )
316 return _coder_nudge(resumed)
317
318 report, result = await self._worker_call(
319 partial(_coder_nudge, result), recover=_coder_nudge_recover
320 )
321 self._persist_coder_usage()
322
323 if report.status == "needs_input":
324 # The coder-question channel: escalate, and on an answer resume the
325 # same coder warm without counting a revision round (clarifications
326 # never trip the breaker; token usage still accumulates).
327 resumed = await self._resolve_needs_input(report)
328 if resumed is None:
329 return False # downgraded / unescalated → a rewrite already happened
330 result = resumed
331 continue
332
333 rounds += 1
334 report_path = self.deps.store.save_group_artifact(
335 self.gid, artifact_name("report", self.generation, rounds), report
336 )
337 self._spread(report.surprises)
338 if report.status == "permission_denied":
339 # Typed denial (plan U3): interrupted, not failed, and no rewrite
340 # spent — bypasses _on_coder_stuck/_rewrite entirely.
341 #
342 # Attributed (plan P2), because one status covered three unrelated
343 # causes with three different remedies and the last validation
344 # misdiagnosed one of them. The kind rides in the exception message
345 # as well as on the instance: the scheduler already writes
346 # `f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"` into `state.json`, so `status`
347 # and the Observatory gain it with no schema change anywhere.
348 kind = classify_denial(
349 denied_command=report.denied_command,
350 denial_error=report.denial_error,
351 denial_source=report.denial_source,
352 deny_rules=self.deps.runner.effective_disallowed_tools(),
353 observed=result.deny_signals,
354 )
355 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended (permission_denied: {kind})")
356 self._log(f"group {self.gid} denial: {denial_remedy(kind)}")
357 raise PermissionDenied(
358 f"group {self.gid} denied command ({kind}): {report.denied_command}",
359 kind=str(kind),
360 denied_command=report.denied_command,
361 denial_error=report.denial_error,
362 denial_source=report.denial_source,
363 )
364 if report.status != "completed":
365 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended (coder {report.status})")
366 await self._on_coder_stuck(report, report_path)
367 return False
368
369 # The verification gate (run r20260829-162627 P1): a `completed`
370 # report that does not carry a passing result for every *required*
371 # item never reaches a reviewer, and never reaches the merge. It
372 # becomes an ordinary `changes_required` round instead — same
373 # breaker, same handoff, same revision prompt — so the coder gets
374 # told exactly which items it left unmet. This is the only thing
375 # standing between a self_verify group and an unchecked merge:
376 # `_review_round` creates no reviewer for that tier, so without it
377 # the coder's own `status` field is the entire gate.
378 gaps = unmet_required_verification(self.group.verification, report.verification_results)
379 if gaps:
380 verdict = ReviewerVerdict(
381 status="changes_required",
382 required_changes=gaps,
383 notes=(
384 "verification gate: the report claims completed but does not "
385 "report a passing result for every required verification item"
386 ),
387 )
388 verdict_path = self.deps.store.save_group_artifact(
389 self.gid, artifact_name("verdict", self.generation, rounds), verdict
390 )
391 self._log(
392 f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: verification gate held "
393 f"({len(gaps)} required item(s) unmet)"
394 )
395 else:
396 verdict, verdict_path = await self._review_round(report_path, rounds)
397 if verdict is None or verdict.status == "approved":
398 outcome = "self-verified" if verdict is None else "approved"
399 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended ({outcome})")
400 # A surprise named this group while it was in review: a
401 # rewrite-worthy one means its pending approval is not accepted
402 # (plan U7 scenario); an informational-only one is noted and the
403 # approval proceeds (plan U13).
404 if await self._handle_pending_surprises("surprise named this group during review"):
405 return False
406 await self._approve_gate(
407 EscalationKind.MERGE_APPROVE, f"merge group {self.gid} ({self.group.name})?"
408 )
409 return await self._merge()
410 if verdict.status in ("too_hard", "structural"):
411 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended ({verdict.status})")
412 await self._on_reviewer_hard(verdict, verdict_path)
413 return False
414
415 # changes_required — breaker gate before the next warm round
416 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended (changes_required)")
417 reason = self._breaker_reason(rounds)
418 if reason:
419 await self._retire(reason)
420 self._prepare_handoff(report, verdict)
421 return False
422 assert verdict_path is not None
423 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.RUNNING)
424 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds + 1)}: started")
425 self._heartbeat.mark_round(self.generation, rounds + 1)
426 revision_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry)
427 result = await self._worker_call(
428 partial(
429 self.deps.runner.resume,
430 session_id=self.coder_sid,
431 prompt=render_revision_prompt(str(verdict_path), verdict.required_changes),
432 cwd=self.workspace,
433 on_turn=revision_on_turn,
434 ),
435 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
436 session_id=sid,
437 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
438 cwd=self.workspace,
439 on_turn=revision_on_turn,
440 ),
441 )
442
443 # ------------------------------------------------------------ re-entry (R4–R6)
444
445 def _find_reentry_session(self) -> SessionEntry | None:
446 """The interrupted coder to warm-resume, discovered from the manifest: the
447 group's latest coder entry at the persisted generation with no retirement
448 reason (spec discovery rule)."""
449 group_entry = self.deps.manifest.groups.get(self.gid)
450 if group_entry is None:
451 return None
452 live = [
453 entry
454 for entry in group_entry.sessions
455 if entry.role == SessionRole.CODER
456 and entry.generation == self.generation
457 and entry.retirement_reason is None
458 ]
459 if not live:
460 return None
461 entry = live[-1]
462 if entry.spec_sha256 is not None and entry.spec_sha256 != _spec_hash(self.group):
463 # The spec was rewritten under the session (an operator wrote a
464 # spec-genN.json after it started): a warm resume would keep a coder
465 # working to a spec nobody holds any more. Fresh coder, new spec.
466 self._reentry_fallback(entry, "spec rewritten since the session started")
467 return None
468 return entry
469
470 async def _reenter(self, entry: SessionEntry, *, round_no: int) -> RoundResult | None:
471 """Warm-resume the interrupted coder in its worktree (R4). Returns the
472 resumed round, or None to fall through to a fresh fork from base — when
473 the persisted context already exceeds the breaker limit (R5) or the warm
474 resume itself fails at the envelope. A SessionError from that fork
475 propagates: the group lands interrupted again, since the envelope is
476 still failing (no in-run retry loop). Exactly one re-entry lifecycle
477 line is written either way (R6).
478
479 ``round_no`` is the number this re-entry carries, announced *before* the
480 blocking resume: the resume performs a whole round's work, so labelling
481 the window `round 0` / `resuming the interrupted coder` for its entire
482 duration hid twenty minutes of real progress from the operator."""
483 assert self.workspace is not None
484 limit = self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit
485 if entry.last_context_tokens > limit:
486 self._reentry_fallback(
487 entry, f"context tokens {entry.last_context_tokens} exceed limit {limit}"
488 )
489 return None
490 # Same reasoning as the fork line: the resume blocks while the worker
491 # reloads its context (14 minutes on the run that prompted this), and
492 # announcing it only on success made a resumed run look wedged.
493 #
494 # Deliberately not phrased as a "re-entry" line: R6 promises exactly one
495 # of those per re-entry and they report an *outcome* (resumed, or forked
496 # after a failure). This one announces an attempt, so it must not be
497 # mistaken for the outcome by a reader counting them.
498 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: resuming interrupted coder session {entry.session_id}")
499 # Ordering matters and is load-bearing: `mark_round` calls
500 # `mark_phase("running")` internally, so marking the round *after* the
501 # phase would overwrite "resuming the interrupted coder" with "running",
502 # and marking the phase after the round would undo this whole fix.
503 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(round_no)}: started")
504 self._heartbeat.mark_round(self.generation, round_no)
505 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("resuming the interrupted coder")
506 reentry_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(entry)
507 try:
508 result = await self._worker_call(
509 partial(
510 self.deps.runner.resume,
511 session_id=entry.session_id,
512 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
513 cwd=self.workspace,
514 on_turn=reentry_on_turn,
515 ),
516 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
517 session_id=sid,
518 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
519 cwd=self.workspace,
520 on_turn=reentry_on_turn,
521 ),
522 )
523 except UsageLimit:
524 # Not a fallback case. The fallback exists for a session that has
525 # become unreachable, where a fresh fork is a real second chance; a
526 # usage limit is the account being out of budget, so the fork fails
527 # identically and spends a generation of the breaker's budget on a call
528 # that could not have succeeded. Propagating leaves the group
529 # INTERRUPTED at this generation, which a plain `resume` re-enters
530 # once the limit has reset.
531 raise
532 except SessionError as exc:
533 self._reentry_fallback(entry, f"warm resume failed: {exc}")
534 return None
535 self.coder_sid = entry.session_id
536 self.coder_entry = entry
537 self.reviewer_sid = None
538 self.sessions_spawned += 1 # live session again: a later rewrite respawns fresh
539 # A warm resume can be the first time this session's transcript actually
540 # exists on disk — the entry was pre-registered before any turn ran, so
541 # its `transcript_path` may still be null until this resume creates the
542 # file. Refreshed here rather than left to the next `_persist_coder_usage`
543 # call, which never touches `transcript_path` at all.
544 self._refresh_transcript(entry)
545 self._log(f"group {self.gid} re-entry: resumed session {entry.session_id}")
546 return result
547
548 def _launch_call(self) -> Callable[..., RoundResult]:
549 """How a *first* round is launched, with its parent context bound.
550
551 The two launch sites (coder and reviewer) call this rather than
552 duplicating the branch: a fresh session primed with the run's base
553 context (the default), or the legacy fork of the run's base session
554 (ADR 0007). Both take the same ``prompt``/``name``/``cwd`` keywords
555 from there on.
556 """
557 if self.deps.fork_base_session:
558 return partial(self.deps.runner.start_fork, base_id=self.deps.base_session_id)
559 return partial(self.deps.runner.start_worker, base_context=self.deps.base_context)
560
561 def _reentry_fallback(self, entry: SessionEntry, reason: str) -> None:
562 """Retire the unreachable session and log the fork decision; the caller
563 falls through to the fresh-fork path (existing handoff-free coder prompt)."""
564 entry.retirement_reason = f"re-entry fallback: {reason}"
565 self._log(f"group {self.gid} re-entry: forked generation {self.generation} ({reason})")
566
567 # ------------------------------------------------------------ outcomes
568
569 def _breaker_reason(self, rounds: int) -> str | None:
570 if rounds >= self.deps.breaker.max_rounds_per_generation:
571 return f"round threshold reached ({rounds} rounds this generation)"
572 context = self.deps.runner.usage_of(self.coder_sid).last_context_tokens
573 if context > self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit:
574 return (
575 f"context tokens {context} exceeded limit {self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit}"
576 )
577 return None
578
579 async def _retire(self, reason: str) -> None:
580 assert self.coder_entry is not None
581 self.coder_entry.retirement_reason = reason
582 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
583 self._log_coder_session_end()
584 self._log(f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: coder retired ({reason})")
585 if self.generation >= self.deps.breaker.max_generations:
586 # Terminal give-up: escalate before failing. An answer grants one more
587 # (guided) generation; None fails as before.
588 response = await self._escalate(
589 EscalationKind.CAPS_EXHAUSTED,
590 prompt=(
591 f"group {self.gid}: generation cap ({self.deps.breaker.max_generations}) "
592 f"exhausted — {reason}"
593 ),
594 want_diff=True,
595 )
596 if response is None:
597 raise GroupFailure(
598 f"generation cap ({self.deps.breaker.max_generations}) exhausted: {reason}"
599 )
600 # `answer` and `retry` alike grant the one extra generation.
601 self._grant_notes.append(f"[operator] {response.answer}")
602 else:
603 # interactive tier only: approve the breaker respawn.
604 await self._approve_gate(
605 EscalationKind.RESPAWN,
606 f"respawn group {self.gid} at generation {self.generation + 1}?",
607 )
608 self._advance_generation()
609
610 def _prepare_handoff(self, report: CoderReport, verdict: ReviewerVerdict) -> None:
611 assert self.workspace is not None
612 items = [f"- {change}" for change in verdict.required_changes]
613 items += [f"- {note}" for note in self._grant_notes] # operator guidance, if any
614 self._grant_notes = []
615 outstanding = "\n".join(items)
616 self.handoff_prompt = render_handoff_prompt(
617 self.deps.run_id,
618 self.group,
619 generation=self.generation,
620 retirement_reason=self.coder_entry.retirement_reason or "retired",
621 last_report=report.model_dump_json(indent=2),
622 outstanding=outstanding,
623 diff_summary=diff_stat(self.workspace, self.deps.base_ref_for(self.group)),
624 decisions=self._decisions_text(),
625 )

112class _ContentFilterStop(Exception):
113 """Loop-internal signal (plan U10): `_worker_call` converts a
114 `ContentFiltered` into this before it can reach a caller's own
115 `except SessionError` — deliberately *not* a `SessionError` subclass, so
116 `_reenter`'s fallback (which catches `SessionError`) never mistakes a
117 content-filtered session for merely unreachable. `_run_generation`
118 catches it once, at the top of every generation."""
119
120 def __init__(self, exc: ContentFiltered):
121 super().__init__(str(exc))
122 self.exc = exc
123

265222
266 async def _worker_call(self, thunk: Callable[[], object], *, recover: Callable[[str], object]):
267 """Runs one worker call in a thread; on a Suspend Cure (plan U5) — the
268 liveness probe having killed this child because it showed no Sign of
269 Life since a detected machine wake — logs the recovery and re-issues
270 ``recover(cured_session_id)`` in *this call's* place, itself routed
271 back through ``_worker_call`` so a second cure re-issues again until
272 the probe's own per-generation cap stops curing. Coder call sites pass
273 a ``recover`` that warm-resumes with the re-entry prompt; reviewer
274 sites pass one that resumes with the re-review prompt (per the U5
275 decision) — the wrapper itself is role-agnostic.
276
277 A ``ContentFiltered`` (plan U10) is converted here to a loop-internal
278 ``_ContentFilterStop`` before it can reach a caller's own
279 ``except SessionError`` — most importantly ``_reenter``'s fallback,
280 which must never treat a content-filtered session as merely
281 unreachable and fork a fresh one from it. Any other exception — a
282 plain ``SessionError``, ``UsageLimit`` — propagates unchanged; this
283 wrapper is transparent to everything but ``SuspendCured`` and
284 ``ContentFiltered``. A ``SuspendCured`` from a first launch whose
285 session never registered on disk still carries a real ``session_id``
286 (read off the argv the failed call actually used, not off the
287 transcript), so ``recover`` resumes it the same as any other cure;
288 being a ``SessionError`` subclass, it would fall through to the
289 ordinary failure handling regardless if it ever turned up somewhere
290 this wrapper does not reach.
291 """
292 try:
293 return await asyncio.to_thread(thunk)
294 except ContentFiltered as exc:
295 raise _ContentFilterStop(exc) from exc
296 except SuspendCured as exc:
297 self._log(
298 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: "
299 f"warm-resuming session {exc.session_id} after suspend cure"
300 )
301 return await self._worker_call(partial(recover, exc.session_id), recover=recover)
302
303 async def run(self) -> GroupState:
304 # interactive tier only: approve before anything is launched.
305 await self._approve_gate(
306 EscalationKind.GROUP_START, f"launch group {self.gid} ({self.group.name})?"
307 )
308 await self._handle_pending_surprises("upstream surprise named this group before launch")
309 self.workspace = self.deps.workspace_for(self.group)
310 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: worktree ready at {self.workspace}")
311 if self.deps.provisioning_failure_for is not None:
312 self._env_failure = self.deps.provisioning_failure_for(self.group)
313 self._heartbeat.start()
314 # A usage-limit pause is announced on this group's heartbeat for as long
315 # as the group is live (see `UsageLimitGate.watch`) — a run that has
316 # stopped because the account is out of budget must read as *paused*,
317 # not as wedged, on the board as well as in the log.
318 gate = getattr(self.deps.runner, "gate", None)
319 if gate is not None:
320 gate.watch(self._heartbeat)
321 try:
322 while True:
323 merged = await self._run_generation()
324 if merged:
325 self._log_coder_session_end()
326 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: completed")
327 return GroupState.COMPLETED
328 # a rewrite or a retirement happened inside; loop spawns the next session
329 finally:
330 if gate is not None:
331 gate.unwatch(self._heartbeat)
332 self._heartbeat.stop()
333
334 # ------------------------------------------------------------ generation
335
336 async def _run_generation(self) -> bool:
337 """One coder session's lifetime. True → merged; False → respawn/rewritten.
338
339 A ``_ContentFilterStop`` (plan U10) can surface from any worker call
340 this generation makes — first launch, coder nudge, needs_input
341 resume, revision resume, or a reviewer call inside ``_review_round``
342 — so it is caught here, at the one place that wraps every one of
343 them, rather than at each call site individually.
344 """
345 try:
346 return await self._run_generation_body()
347 except _ContentFilterStop as exc:
348 await self._on_content_filtered(exc.exc)
349 return False
350
351 async def _run_generation_body(self) -> bool:
352 assert self.workspace is not None
353 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.RUNNING)
354 first: RoundResult | None = None
355 reentry, self._reentry_entry = self._reentry_entry, None # one-shot
356 is_reentry = reentry is not None
357 self._flake_reruns = 0
358 # Re-entry (warm-resumed or fallback-forked) continues this generation's
359 # numbering rather than starting over, so round-numbered artifacts don't
360 # collide with — and silently overwrite — pre-crash ones still on disk.
361 #
362 # Computed *before* the re-entry call, not after (plan P3): the re-entry
363 # resume is itself a full round — it writes files and runs tests, for
364 # twenty minutes on the run that prompted this — so it has to be able to
365 # announce its own number before it blocks. `completed_round_count` reads
366 # only the report artifacts already on disk and takes nothing from the
367 # resume, so hoisting it changes no number.
368 rounds = (
369 completed_round_count(self.deps.store.paths, self.gid, self.generation)
370 if is_reentry
371 else 0
372 )
373 if reentry is not None:
374 first = await self._reenter(reentry, round_no=rounds + 1)
375 if first is None:
376 prompt = self.handoff_prompt or render_coder_prompt(
377 self.deps.run_id, self.group, decisions=self._decisions_text()
378 )
379 prompt = self._apply_briefing(prompt)
380 prompt = self._apply_env_notice(prompt)
381 prompt = self._apply_operator_note(prompt)
382 self.handoff_prompt = None
383 # The session id is generated and recorded *before* the blocking fork
384 # call, not after (plan U7): a crash mid-call would otherwise leave no
385 # manifest entry for a group interrupted during its very first round,
386 # so a later resume would fork a brand new session instead of finding
387 # the one already under way.
388 self.coder_sid = str(uuid.uuid4())
389 self.reviewer_sid = None
390 self.coder_entry = self._record(SessionRole.CODER, self.coder_sid)
391 self.coder_entry.spec_sha256 = _spec_hash(self.group)
392 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
393 # Logged *before* the fork, not after. `start_fork` blocks for as long
394 # as the base session takes to absorb the group's prompt — 21 minutes
395 # on a real run — and the old "coder launched" line landed only once it
396 # returned, so a group killed mid-launch left a log that never
397 # mentioned it had started, and a live run showed a silent gap with no
398 # indication anything was happening.
399 launch = "forking base session" if self.deps.fork_base_session else "fresh session"
400 self._log(
401 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: "
402 f"coder launching, {launch} (session {self.coder_sid})"
403 )
404 # `round N: started` logged and marked *before* the fork call, not
405 # after — matching `_reenter`'s pattern. `start_fork` is itself round

409 # round at all.
410 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds + 1)}: started")
411 self._heartbeat.mark_round(self.generation, rounds + 1)
412 self._heartbeat.mark_phase(
413 "forking the base session" if self.deps.fork_base_session else "starting the coder"
414 )
415 self._watch_transcript(self.coder_entry)
416 coder_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry)
417 first = await self._worker_call(
418 partial(
419 self._launch_call(),
420 prompt=prompt,
421 name=session_display_name(self.deps.run_id, self.gid, "coder", self.generation),
422 cwd=self.workspace,
423 session_id=self.coder_sid,
424 on_turn=coder_on_turn,
425 ),
426 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
427 session_id=sid,
428 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
429 cwd=self.workspace,
430 on_turn=coder_on_turn,
431 ),
432 )
433 self._adopt_actual_session_id(first)
434 self._refresh_transcript(self.coder_entry)
435 self._log(f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: coder launched")
436 result = first

465 on_turn=self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry),

513 denial_source=report.denial_source,
514 )

525 # told exactly which items it left unmet. This is the only thing

532 status="changes_required",
533 required_changes=gaps,
534 notes=(
535 "verification gate: the report claims completed but does not "
536 "report a passing result for every required verification item"
537 ),
538 )
539 verdict_path = self.deps.store.save_group_artifact(
540 self.gid, artifact_name("verdict", self.generation, rounds), verdict
541 )
542 self._log(
543 f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: verification gate held "
544 f"({len(gaps)} required item(s) unmet)"
545 )
546 else:
547 verdict, verdict_path = await self._review_round(report_path, rounds)
548 if verdict is None or verdict.status == "approved":

550 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended ({outcome})")

553 # (plan U7 scenario); an informational-only one is noted and the
554 # approval proceeds (plan U13).

558 EscalationKind.MERGE_APPROVE, f"merge group {self.gid} ({self.group.name})?"
559 )
560 return await self._merge()

562 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds)}: ended ({verdict.status})")

572 return False
573 assert verdict_path is not None
574 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.RUNNING)
575 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(rounds + 1)}: started")
576 self._heartbeat.mark_round(self.generation, rounds + 1)
577 revision_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(self.coder_entry)
578 result = await self._worker_call(
579 partial(
580 self.deps.runner.resume,
581 session_id=self.coder_sid,
582 prompt=render_revision_prompt(str(verdict_path), verdict.required_changes),
583 cwd=self.workspace,
584 on_turn=revision_on_turn,
585 ),
586 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
587 session_id=sid,
588 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
589 cwd=self.workspace,
590 on_turn=revision_on_turn,
591 ),
592 )

594 # ------------------------------------------------------------ re-entry (R4–R6)
595
596 def _find_reentry_session(self) -> SessionEntry | None:
597 """The interrupted coder to warm-resume, discovered from the manifest: the
598 group's latest coder entry at the persisted generation with no retirement
599 reason (spec discovery rule)."""
600 group_entry = self.deps.manifest.groups.get(self.gid)
601 if group_entry is None:
602 return None
603 live = [
604 entry
605 for entry in group_entry.sessions
606 if entry.role == SessionRole.CODER
607 and entry.generation == self.generation
608 and entry.retirement_reason is None
609 ]
610 if not live:
611 return None
612 entry = live[-1]
613 if entry.spec_sha256 is not None and entry.spec_sha256 != _spec_hash(self.group):
614 # The spec was rewritten under the session (an operator wrote a
615 # spec-genN.json after it started): a warm resume would keep a coder
616 # working to a spec nobody holds any more. Fresh coder, new spec.
617 self._reentry_fallback(entry, "spec rewritten since the session started")
618 return None
619 return entry
620
621 async def _reenter(self, entry: SessionEntry, *, round_no: int) -> RoundResult | None:
622 """Warm-resume the interrupted coder in its worktree (R4). Returns the
623 resumed round, or None to fall through to a fresh fork from base — when
624 the persisted context already exceeds the breaker limit (R5) or the warm
625 resume itself fails at the envelope. A SessionError from that fork
626 propagates: the group lands interrupted again, since the envelope is
627 still failing (no in-run retry loop). Exactly one re-entry lifecycle
628 line is written either way (R6).
629
630 ``round_no`` is the number this re-entry carries, announced *before* the
631 blocking resume: the resume performs a whole round's work, so labelling
632 the window `round 0` / `resuming the interrupted coder` for its entire
633 duration hid twenty minutes of real progress from the operator."""
634 assert self.workspace is not None
635 limit = self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit
636 if entry.last_context_tokens > limit:
637 self._reentry_fallback(
638 entry, f"context tokens {entry.last_context_tokens} exceed limit {limit}"
639 )
640 return None
641 # Same reasoning as the fork line: the resume blocks while the worker
642 # reloads its context (14 minutes on the run that prompted this), and
643 # announcing it only on success made a resumed run look wedged.
644 #
645 # Deliberately not phrased as a "re-entry" line: R6 promises exactly one
646 # of those per re-entry and they report an *outcome* (resumed, or forked
647 # after a failure). This one announces an attempt, so it must not be
648 # mistaken for the outcome by a reader counting them.
649 self._log(f"group {self.gid}: resuming interrupted coder session {entry.session_id}")
650 # Ordering matters and is load-bearing: `mark_round` calls
651 # `mark_phase("running")` internally, so marking the round *after* the
652 # phase would overwrite "resuming the interrupted coder" with "running",
653 # and marking the phase after the round would undo this whole fix.
654 self._log(f"{self._round_tag(round_no)}: started")
655 self._heartbeat.mark_round(self.generation, round_no)
656 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("resuming the interrupted coder")
657 reentry_on_turn = self._make_coder_on_turn(entry)
658 try:
659 result = await self._worker_call(
660 partial(
661 self.deps.runner.resume,
662 session_id=entry.session_id,
663 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
664 cwd=self.workspace,
665 on_turn=reentry_on_turn,
666 ),
667 recover=lambda sid: self.deps.runner.resume(
668 session_id=sid,
669 prompt=render_reentry_prompt(self.group),
670 cwd=self.workspace,
671 on_turn=reentry_on_turn,
672 ),
673 )
674 except UsageLimit:
675 # Not a fallback case. The fallback exists for a session that has
676 # become unreachable, where a fresh fork is a real second chance; a
677 # usage limit is the account being out of budget, so the fork fails
678 # identically and spends a generation of the breaker's budget on a call
679 # that could not have succeeded. Propagating leaves the group
680 # INTERRUPTED at this generation, which a plain `resume` re-enters
681 # once the limit has reset.
682 raise
683 except SessionError as exc:
684 self._reentry_fallback(entry, f"warm resume failed: {exc}")
685 return None
686 self.coder_sid = entry.session_id
687 self.coder_entry = entry
688 self.reviewer_sid = None
689 self.sessions_spawned += 1 # live session again: a later rewrite respawns fresh
690 # A warm resume can be the first time this session's transcript actually
691 # exists on disk — the entry was pre-registered before any turn ran, so
692 # its `transcript_path` may still be null until this resume creates the
693 # file. Refreshed here rather than left to the next `_persist_coder_usage`
694 # call, which never touches `transcript_path` at all.
695 self._refresh_transcript(entry)
696 self._log(f"group {self.gid} re-entry: resumed session {entry.session_id}")
697 return result
698
699 def _launch_call(self) -> Callable[..., RoundResult]:
700 """How a *first* round is launched, with its parent context bound.
701
702 The two launch sites (coder and reviewer) call this rather than
703 duplicating the branch: a fresh session primed with the run's base
704 context (the default), or the legacy fork of the run's base session
705 (ADR 0007). Both take the same ``prompt``/``name``/``cwd`` keywords
706 from there on.
707 """
708 if self.deps.fork_base_session:
709 return partial(self.deps.runner.start_fork, base_id=self.deps.base_session_id)
710 return partial(self.deps.runner.start_worker, base_context=self.deps.base_context)
711
712 def _reentry_fallback(self, entry: SessionEntry, reason: str) -> None:
713 """Retire the unreachable session and log the fork decision; the caller
714 falls through to the fresh-fork path (existing handoff-free coder prompt)."""
715 entry.retirement_reason = f"re-entry fallback: {reason}"
716 self._log(f"group {self.gid} re-entry: forked generation {self.generation} ({reason})")
717
718 # ------------------------------------------------------------ review
719
720 # ------------------------------------------------------------ outcomes
721
722 def _breaker_reason(self, rounds: int) -> str | None:
723 if rounds >= self.deps.breaker.max_rounds_per_generation:
724 return f"round threshold reached ({rounds} rounds this generation)"
725 context = self.deps.runner.usage_of(self.coder_sid).last_context_tokens
726 if context > self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit:
727 return (
728 f"context tokens {context} exceeded limit {self.deps.breaker.context_token_limit}"
729 )
730 return None
731
732 async def _retire(self, reason: str) -> None:
733 assert self.coder_entry is not None
734 self.coder_entry.retirement_reason = reason
735 self.deps.store.save(self.deps.manifest)
736 self._log_coder_session_end()
737 self._log(f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: coder retired ({reason})")
738 if self.generation >= self.deps.breaker.max_generations:
739 # Terminal give-up: escalate before failing. An answer grants one more
740 # (guided) generation; None fails as before.
741 response = await self._escalate(
742 EscalationKind.CAPS_EXHAUSTED,
743 prompt=(
744 f"group {self.gid}: generation cap ({self.deps.breaker.max_generations}) "
745 f"exhausted — {reason}"
746 ),
747 want_diff=True,
748 )
749 if response is None:
750 raise GroupFailure(
751 f"generation cap ({self.deps.breaker.max_generations}) exhausted: {reason}"
752 )
753 # `answer` and `retry` alike grant the one extra generation.
754 self._grant_notes.append(f"[operator] {response.answer}")
755 else:
756 # interactive tier only: approve the breaker respawn.
757 await self._approve_gate(
758 EscalationKind.RESPAWN,
759 f"respawn group {self.gid} at generation {self.generation + 1}?",
760 )
761 self._advance_generation()
762
763 def _prepare_handoff(self, report: CoderReport, verdict: ReviewerVerdict) -> None:
764 assert self.workspace is not None
765 items = [f"- {change}" for change in verdict.required_changes]
766 items += [f"- {note}" for note in self._grant_notes] # operator guidance, if any
767 self._grant_notes = []
768 outstanding = "\n".join(items)
769 self.handoff_prompt = render_handoff_prompt(
770 self.deps.run_id,
771 self.group,
772 generation=self.generation,
773 retirement_reason=self.coder_entry.retirement_reason or "retired",
774 last_report=report.model_dump_json(indent=2),
775 outstanding=outstanding,
776 diff_summary=diff_stat(self.workspace, self.deps.base_ref_for(self.group)),
777 decisions=self._decisions_text(),
778 )
779
780 # ------------------------------------------------------------ escalation
781
782 def _log(self, text: str) -> None:223 def _log(self, text: str) -> None:
783 """Append to the run's always-on lifecycle log (R10): control-plane events224 """Append to the run's always-on lifecycle log (R10): control-plane events
784 land in ``run.log`` in every run mode, HITL or autonomous."""225 land in ``run.log`` in every run mode, HITL or autonomous."""
